God, the Exalted, says: We have placed these people, who are destined for wretchedness, in a condition where their path to guidance is like the condition of one who has a shackle placed on his neck, so that his two hands are gathered together with his neck beneath his chin, and his head is raised, so that he becomes *muqmah*. For this reason He said: ﴿so they are *muqmahun*﴾. *Al-muqmah* is the one who raises his head. Umm Zar' said in her speech: "I drink and then *atqammah*," meaning: I drink until I am quenched, and I raise my head in contentment and satisfaction. He mentioned only the shackle on the neck and did not mention the hands, although the hands are intended, just as the poet said [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (22/98).]]:

*I do not know, when I set out for a land seeking good, which of the two will come upon me:*
*Is it the good that I seek, or the evil that does not leave me alone?*

He mentioned the good and left out the evil, since the context and the speech indicate it. Likewise here, since the shackle is only recognized as binding the hands together with the neck, He mentioned the neck and left out the hands.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they reach up to the chins, so they are *muqmahun*﴾. He said: This is like God's saying: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ [al-Isra' 29]. He means by this that their hands are bound to their necks, so they cannot extend them toward goodness.

Mujahid said: ﴿so they are *muqmahun*﴾: they are raising their heads, and their hands are placed over their mouths, so they are shackled from every good.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier﴾. Mujahid said: a barrier against the truth. ﴿And behind them a barrier﴾, Mujahid said: against the truth, so they wander about aimlessly. Qatadah said: a barrier against misguidance.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So We covered them﴾, that is, We covered their sight from the truth. ﴿So they do not see﴾, that is, they do not benefit from any good and are not guided to it.

Ibn Jarir said: It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to read: "*fa-a'shaynahum*" with the unpointed letter 'ayn, from *al-'asha*, which is a disease of the eye.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: God placed this barrier between them and Islam and faith, so they cannot reach it. He recited: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97]. Then he said: Whom God prevents, no one can guide.

'Ikrimah said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad, I will certainly do such-and-such to him," so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks﴾ up to His words ﴿[so] they do not see﴾. He said: They used to say: "This is Muhammad," and then they would say: "Where is he? Where is he?" They could not see him. Related by Ibn Jarir.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ziyad narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Abu Jahl said while they were sitting: "Muhammad claims that if you follow him you will become kings, and when you die you will be resurrected after your death, and you will have gardens better than the gardens of Jordan. And if you oppose him, there will be slaughter for you, and then you will be resurrected after your death, and there will be a fire for you in which you will be tormented." At that moment the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came out to them, holding a handful of dust, and God had blinded their eyes to him. He began to scatter it over their heads while reciting: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an﴾, until he reached His words: ﴿And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see﴾. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) then went off to attend to his need, and they stayed watching at his door. Then a man came out of the house to them after that and said: "What is wrong with you?" They said: "We are waiting for Muhammad." He said: "He has already come out to you." Not one man among them remained without having dust placed on his head. Then he went off to his need, and each one of them began to shake off the dust from his head. He said: The words of Abu Jahl reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "I too say that: for them there is slaughter from me, and he is one of them."

* *

As for His words: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, that is: God has sealed them with misguidance, so warning does not benefit them, and they are not affected by it.

Its like has already been mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, at the commentary on the sixth verse. And as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, and even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97].

﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder﴾, that is: only the believers who follow the Reminder, which is the Great Qur'an, benefit from your warning. ﴿And fears the Most Merciful﴾, that is: in a place where no one sees him except God, he knows that God is watching over him and is aware of what he does. ﴿So give him good news of forgiveness﴾, that is: for his sins, ﴿and a noble reward﴾, that is: a great, abundant, good, and beautiful reward, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk 12].

Then God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life﴾, that is: on the Day of Resurrection. This also contains an indication that God, the Exalted, gives life to the hearts of whichever disbelievers He wills, whose hearts have died through misguidance, and then guides them to the truth, as He, the Exalted, said after mentioning the hardness of hearts: ﴿Know that God gives life to the earth after its death. We have made the signs clear to you, so that you may understand﴾ [al-Hadid 17].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward﴾, that is: of deeds.

Regarding His words: ﴿and their traces﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: We record their deeds which they performed themselves, and their traces which they left after them, and We will recompense them for those as well, whether good or evil, as in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam, he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it after him, without any reduction from their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, he will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it after him, without any reduction from their burdens."

Related by Muslim, through the narration of Shu'bah, from 'Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, may God be pleased with him, and in it is the story of the people in woolen cloaks from Mudar [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1017.]]. Ibn Abi Hatim related it from his father, from Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Ju'fi, from Abu al-Muhayyat Yahya ibn Ya'la, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, and he mentioned the hadith in full, then recited this verse: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾.

Muslim also related it through the narration of Abu 'Awanah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father, and mentioned it [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1017.]]. Likewise is the other hadith in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him" [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1631.]].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard Mujahid say concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾: "What they left behind of misguidance."

Ibn Lahi'ah said, from 'Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾: he means what they left as a legacy. He says: What they established of a practice, which a people then acted upon after their death. If it was good, then he has the like of their rewards, without any reduction from the reward of the one who did it. And if it was evil, then upon him is the like of their burdens, without any reduction from the burden of the one who did it. Related by Ibn Abi Hatim, both of these.

This second view is the one chosen by al-Baghawi [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (7/9).]].

The second view: that what is meant by this is the traces of their steps toward obedience or disobedience.

Ibn Abi Najih and others said, from Mujahid: ﴿What they sent forward﴾: their deeds. ﴿And their traces﴾: he said: their steps with their feet. Likewise al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿And their traces﴾ means their steps. Qatadah said: If God, the Exalted, were to neglect anything of your affairs, O son of Adam, He would neglect what the winds erase of these traces. But He has counted for the son of Adam his trace and all his deeds, to the extent that He has counted even this trace in what is obedience to God or disobedience to Him. So whoever among you is able to record his trace in obedience to God, let him do so.

Several hadiths have been related with this meaning:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The areas around the mosque became empty, so the Banu Salamah wanted to move close to the mosque. This reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said to them: "It has reached me that you intend to move close to the mosque." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, we have intended that." He said: "O Banu Salamah, stay in your homes, your traces will be recorded; stay in your homes, your traces will be recorded."

Muslim related it likewise, through the hadith of Sa'id al-Juraydi and Kahmas ibn al-Hasan, both from Abu Nadrah, whose name is al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qut'ah al-'Abdi, from Jabir [[Musnad Ahmad (3/332) and Sahih Muslim, no. 665.]].

The second hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Wasiti narrated to us, Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Sufyan, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Banu Salamah were in a part of Madinah, and they wanted to move to a place near the mosque, so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Indeed, your traces are being recorded." So they did not move.

Al-Tirmidhi alone related it, in the commentary on this noble verse, from Muhammad ibn al-Wazir, with this chain. Then he said: "Hasan gharib, from the hadith of al-Thawri" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3226.]].

Ibn Jarir related it from Sulayman ibn 'Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Tarif, who is Ibn Shihab Abu Sufyan al-Sa'di, from Abu Nadrah, with this [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/100).]].

It has also been related by a route other than al-Thawri. The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said:

'Abbad ibn Ziyad al-Saji narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Juraydi, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id who said: The Banu Salamah complained to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the distance of their homes from the mosque, so this was revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾, and they remained in their place.

Ibn al-Muthanna also narrated to us: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

In it there is strangeness regarding the mention of the revelation of this verse, while the surah in its entirety is Meccan, and God knows best.

Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Jahḍamī narrated to us: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The dwellings of the Anṣār were far from the mosque, so they wanted to move closer to the mosque. Then this was revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾. So they said: "We will remain in our places." Thus he narrated it, and there is nothing in it that is *marfūʿ* (traced back to the Prophet ﷺ). [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/100).]

Al-Ṭabarānī also narrated it, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam, from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Firyābī, from Isrāʾīl, from Simāk, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Anṣār's dwellings were far from the mosque, so they wanted to relocate closer to the mosque. Then this was revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾, so they remained in their dwellings. [Al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (12/8). Its narrator ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam is weak.]

A man among the people said: "And why, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When a man dies outside his birthplace, a measure of his birthplace is allotted to him in Paradise, up to the place where his traces end."

Al-Nasāʾī narrated it from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, and Ibn Mājah from Ḥarmalah, both from Ibn Wahb, from Ḥayy ibn ʿAbd Allāh, with the same wording. [Al-Musnad (2/177), Sunan al-Nasāʾī (4/7), and Sunan Ibn Mājah, no. 1614.]

Ibn Jarīr (al-Ṭabarī) also said: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us: Abū Tumaylah narrated to us: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, from Thābit, who said: I walked with Anas and quickened my pace, so he took my hand and we walked slowly. When we finished the prayer, Anas said: I walked with Zayd ibn Thābit and quickened my pace, and he said: "O Anas, did you not realise that traces are recorded? Did you not realise that traces are recorded?" [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/100).]

This statement does not contradict the first one. Rather, it draws attention to the same meaning by way of an even stronger and more fitting inference. For if these traces are recorded, then the deeds that set an example for others, whether good or evil, are all the more deserving of being recorded. And Allah knows best.

\* \*

As for His saying: ﴿And We have enumerated all things in a clear register﴾, meaning: all created things are written in a manifest book, preserved in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ*). The "clear register" (*al-Imām al-Mubīn*) here is the Mother of the Book (*Umm al-Kitāb*). This is the view of Mujāhid, Qatādah, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. The same applies to His saying: ﴿On the day We shall call every people with their record﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 71], meaning: with the book of their deeds, which bears witness against them for the good and evil they did. As Allah says: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward﴾ [al-Zumar: 69], and He says: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say: "Woe to us! What kind of book is this? It leaves out nothing small or great but has recorded it all." And they will find what they did present there, and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

God, the Exalted, says: We have placed these people, who are destined for wretchedness, in a condition where their path to guidance is like the condition of one who has a shackle placed on his neck, so that his two hands are gathered together with his neck beneath his chin, and his head is raised, so that he becomes *muqmah*. For this reason He said: ﴿so they are *muqmahun*﴾. *Al-muqmah* is the one who raises his head. Umm Zar' said in her speech: "I drink and then *atqammah*," meaning: I drink until I am quenched, and I raise my head in contentment and satisfaction. He mentioned only the shackle on the neck and did not mention the hands, although the hands are intended, just as the poet said [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (22/98).]]:

*I do not know, when I set out for a land seeking good, which of the two will come upon me:*
*Is it the good that I seek, or the evil that does not leave me alone?*

He mentioned the good and left out the evil, since the context and the speech indicate it. Likewise here, since the shackle is only recognized as binding the hands together with the neck, He mentioned the neck and left out the hands.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they reach up to the chins, so they are *muqmahun*﴾. He said: This is like God's saying: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ [al-Isra' 29]. He means by this that their hands are bound to their necks, so they cannot extend them toward goodness.

Mujahid said: ﴿so they are *muqmahun*﴾: they are raising their heads, and their hands are placed over their mouths, so they are shackled from every good.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier﴾. Mujahid said: a barrier against the truth. ﴿And behind them a barrier﴾, Mujahid said: against the truth, so they wander about aimlessly. Qatadah said: a barrier against misguidance.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So We covered them﴾, that is, We covered their sight from the truth. ﴿So they do not see﴾, that is, they do not benefit from any good and are not guided to it.

Ibn Jarir said: It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to read: "*fa-a'shaynahum*" with the unpointed letter 'ayn, from *al-'asha*, which is a disease of the eye.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: God placed this barrier between them and Islam and faith, so they cannot reach it. He recited: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97]. Then he said: Whom God prevents, no one can guide.

'Ikrimah said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad, I will certainly do such-and-such to him," so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks﴾ up to His words ﴿[so] they do not see﴾. He said: They used to say: "This is Muhammad," and then they would say: "Where is he? Where is he?" They could not see him. Related by Ibn Jarir.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ziyad narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Abu Jahl said while they were sitting: "Muhammad claims that if you follow him you will become kings, and when you die you will be resurrected after your death, and you will have gardens better than the gardens of Jordan. And if you oppose him, there will be slaughter for you, and then you will be resurrected after your death, and there will be a fire for you in which you will be tormented." At that moment the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came out to them, holding a handful of dust, and God had blinded their eyes to him. He began to scatter it over their heads while reciting: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an﴾, until he reached His words: ﴿And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see﴾. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) then went off to attend to his need, and they stayed watching at his door. Then a man came out of the house to them after that and said: "What is wrong with you?" They said: "We are waiting for Muhammad." He said: "He has already come out to you." Not one man among them remained without having dust placed on his head. Then he went off to his need, and each one of them began to shake off the dust from his head. He said: The words of Abu Jahl reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "I too say that: for them there is slaughter from me, and he is one of them."

* *

As for His words: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, that is: God has sealed them with misguidance, so warning does not benefit them, and they are not affected by it.

Its like has already been mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, at the commentary on the sixth verse. And as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, and even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97].

﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder﴾, that is: only the believers who follow the Reminder, which is the Great Qur'an, benefit from your warning. ﴿And fears the Most Merciful﴾, that is: in a place where no one sees him except God, he knows that God is watching over him and is aware of what he does. ﴿So give him good news of forgiveness﴾, that is: for his sins, ﴿and a noble reward﴾, that is: a great, abundant, good, and beautiful reward, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk 12].

Then God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life﴾, that is: on the Day of Resurrection. This also contains an indication that God, the Exalted, gives life to the hearts of whichever disbelievers He wills, whose hearts have died through misguidance, and then guides them to the truth, as He, the Exalted, said after mentioning the hardness of hearts: ﴿Know that God gives life to the earth after its death. We have made the signs clear to you, so that you may understand﴾ [al-Hadid 17].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward﴾, that is: of deeds.

Regarding His words: ﴿and their traces﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: We record their deeds which they performed themselves, and their traces which they left after them, and We will recompense them for those as well, whether good or evil, as in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam, he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it after him, without any reduction from their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, he will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it after him, without any reduction from their burdens."

Related by Muslim, through the narration of Shu'bah, from 'Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, may God be pleased with him, and in it is the story of the people in woolen cloaks from Mudar [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1017.]]. Ibn Abi Hatim related it from his father, from Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Ju'fi, from Abu al-Muhayyat Yahya ibn Ya'la, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, and he mentioned the hadith in full, then recited this verse: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾.

Muslim also related it through the narration of Abu 'Awanah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father, and mentioned it [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1017.]]. Likewise is the other hadith in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him" [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1631.]].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard Mujahid say concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾: "What they left behind of misguidance."

Ibn Lahi'ah said, from 'Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾: he means what they left as a legacy. He says: What they established of a practice, which a people then acted upon after their death. If it was good, then he has the like of their rewards, without any reduction from the reward of the one who did it. And if it was evil, then upon him is the like of their burdens, without any reduction from the burden of the one who did it. Related by Ibn Abi Hatim, both of these.

This second view is the one chosen by al-Baghawi [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (7/9).]].

The second view: that what is meant by this is the traces of their steps toward obedience or disobedience.

Ibn Abi Najih and others said, from Mujahid: ﴿What they sent forward﴾: their deeds. ﴿And their traces﴾: he said: their steps with their feet. Likewise al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿And their traces﴾ means their steps. Qatadah said: If God, the Exalted, were to neglect anything of your affairs, O son of Adam, He would neglect what the winds erase of these traces. But He has counted for the son of Adam his trace and all his deeds, to the extent that He has counted even this trace in what is obedience to God or disobedience to Him. So whoever among you is able to record his trace in obedience to God, let him do so.

Several hadiths have been related with this meaning:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The areas around the mosque became empty, so the Banu Salamah wanted to move close to the mosque. This reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said to them: "It has reached me that you intend to move close to the mosque." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, we have intended that." He said: "O Banu Salamah, stay in your homes, your traces will be recorded; stay in your homes, your traces will be recorded."

Muslim related it likewise, through the hadith of Sa'id al-Juraydi and Kahmas ibn al-Hasan, both from Abu Nadrah, whose name is al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qut'ah al-'Abdi, from Jabir [[Musnad Ahmad (3/332) and Sahih Muslim, no. 665.]].

The second hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Wasiti narrated to us, Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Sufyan, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Banu Salamah were in a part of Madinah, and they wanted to move to a place near the mosque, so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Indeed, your traces are being recorded." So they did not move.

Al-Tirmidhi alone related it, in the commentary on this noble verse, from Muhammad ibn al-Wazir, with this chain. Then he said: "Hasan gharib, from the hadith of al-Thawri" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3226.]].

Ibn Jarir related it from Sulayman ibn 'Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Tarif, who is Ibn Shihab Abu Sufyan al-Sa'di, from Abu Nadrah, with this [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/100).]].

It has also been related by a route other than al-Thawri. The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said:

'Abbad ibn Ziyad al-Saji narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Juraydi, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id who said: The Banu Salamah complained to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the distance of their homes from the mosque, so this was revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾, and they remained in their place.

Ibn al-Muthanna also narrated to us: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

In it there is strangeness regarding the mention of the revelation of this verse, while the surah in its entirety is Meccan, and God knows best.

Related by Muslim, through the narration of Shu'bah, from 'Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, may God be pleased with him, and in it is the story of the people in woolen cloaks from Mudar [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1017.]]. Ibn Abi Hatim related it from his father, from Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Ju'fi, from Abu al-Muhayyat Yahya ibn Ya'la, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, and he mentioned the hadith in full, then recited this verse: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾.

Muslim also related it through the narration of Abu 'Awanah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father, and mentioned it [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1017.]]. Likewise is the other hadith in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him" [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1631.]].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard Mujahid say concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾: "What they left behind of misguidance."

Ibn Lahi'ah said, from 'Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾: he means what they left as a legacy. He says: What they established of a practice, which a people then acted upon after their death. If it was good, then he has the like of their rewards, without any reduction from the reward of the one who did it. And if it was evil, then upon him is the like of their burdens, without any reduction from the burden of the one who did it. Related by Ibn Abi Hatim, both of these.

This second view is the one chosen by al-Baghawi [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (7/9).]].

The second view: that what is meant by this is the traces of their steps toward obedience or disobedience.

Ibn Abi Najih and others said, from Mujahid: ﴿What they sent forward﴾: their deeds. ﴿And their traces﴾: he said: their steps with their feet. Likewise al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿And their traces﴾ means their steps. Qatadah said: If God, the Exalted, were to neglect anything of your affairs, O son of Adam, He would neglect what the winds erase of these traces. But He has counted for the son of Adam his trace and all his deeds, to the extent that He has counted even this trace in what is obedience to God or disobedience to Him. So whoever among you is able to record his trace in obedience to God, let him do so.

Several hadiths have been related with this meaning:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The areas around the mosque became empty, so the Banu Salamah wanted to move close to the mosque. This reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said to them: "It has reached me that you intend to move close to the mosque." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, we have intended that." He said: "O Banu Salamah, stay in your homes, your traces will be recorded; stay in your homes, your traces will be recorded."

Muslim related it likewise, through the hadith of Sa'id al-Juraydi and Kahmas ibn al-Hasan, both from Abu Nadrah, whose name is al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qut'ah al-'Abdi, from Jabir [[Musnad Ahmad (3/332) and Sahih Muslim, no. 665.]].

The second hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Wasiti narrated to us, Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Sufyan, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Banu Salamah were in a part of Madinah, and they wanted to move to a place near the mosque, so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Indeed, your traces are being recorded." So they did not move.

Al-Tirmidhi alone related it, in the commentary on this noble verse, from Muhammad ibn al-Wazir, with this chain. Then he said: "Hasan gharib, from the hadith of al-Thawri" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3226.]].

Ibn Jarir related it from Sulayman ibn 'Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Tarif, who is Ibn Shihab Abu Sufyan al-Sa'di, from Abu Nadrah, with this [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/100).]].

It has also been related by a route other than al-Thawri. The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said:

'Abbad ibn Ziyad al-Saji narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Juraydi, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id who said: The Banu Salamah complained to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the distance of their homes from the mosque, so this was revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾, and they remained in their place.

Ibn al-Muthanna also narrated to us: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

In it there is strangeness regarding the mention of the revelation of this verse, while the surah in its entirety is Meccan, and God knows best.

The third hadith: Ibn Jarir said:

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 36, verses 8–12 (part 2 of 2)**

Thus he narrated it, and there is nothing in it that is *marfūʿ* (traced back to the Prophet ﷺ). [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/100).]

When we finished the prayer, Anas said: I walked with Zayd ibn Thābit and quickened my pace, and he said: "O Anas, did you not realise that traces are recorded? As for His saying: ﴿And We have enumerated all things in a clear register﴾, meaning: all created things are written in a manifest book, preserved in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ*). The "clear register" (*al-Imām al-Mubīn*) here is the Mother of the Book (*Umm al-Kitāb*). This is the view of Mujāhid, Qatādah, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. The same applies to His saying: ﴿On the day We shall call every people with their record﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 71], meaning: with the book of their deeds, which bears witness against them for the good and evil they did. As Allah says: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward﴾ [al-Zumar: 69], and He says: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say: "Woe to us! What kind of book is this? It leaves out nothing small or great but has recorded it all." And they will find what they did present there, and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

God, the Exalted, says: We have placed these people, who are destined for wretchedness, in a condition where their path to guidance is like the condition of one who has a shackle placed on his neck, so that his two hands are gathered together with his neck beneath his chin, and his head is raised, so that he becomes *muqmah*. For this reason He said: ﴿so they are *muqmahun*﴾. *Al-muqmah* is the one who raises his head. Umm Zar' said in her speech: "I drink and then *atqammah*," meaning: I drink until I am quenched, and I raise my head in contentment and satisfaction. He mentioned only the shackle on the neck and did not mention the hands, although the hands are intended, just as the poet said [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (22/98).]]:

*I do not know, when I set out for a land seeking good, which of the two will come upon me:*
*Is it the good that I seek, or the evil that does not leave me alone?*

He mentioned the good and left out the evil, since the context and the speech indicate it. Likewise here, since the shackle is only recognized as binding the hands together with the neck, He mentioned the neck and left out the hands.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they reach up to the chins, so they are *muqmahun*﴾. He said: This is like God's saying: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ [al-Isra' 29]. He means by this that their hands are bound to their necks, so they cannot extend them toward goodness.

Mujahid said: ﴿so they are *muqmahun*﴾: they are raising their heads, and their hands are placed over their mouths, so they are shackled from every good.

As for His words: ﴿And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier﴾. Mujahid said: a barrier against the truth. ﴿And behind them a barrier﴾, Mujahid said: against the truth, so they wander about aimlessly. Qatadah said: a barrier against misguidance.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So We covered them﴾, that is, We covered their sight from the truth. ﴿So they do not see﴾, that is, they do not benefit from any good and are not guided to it.

Ibn Jarir said: It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to read: "*fa-a'shaynahum*" with the unpointed letter 'ayn, from *al-'asha*, which is a disease of the eye.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: God placed this barrier between them and Islam and faith, so they cannot reach it. He recited: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97]. Then he said: Whom God prevents, no one can guide.

'Ikrimah said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad, I will certainly do such-and-such to him," so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks﴾ up to His words ﴿[so] they do not see﴾. He said: They used to say: "This is Muhammad," and then they would say: "Where is he? Where is he?" They could not see him. Related by Ibn Jarir.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ziyad narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Abu Jahl said while they were sitting: "Muhammad claims that if you follow him you will become kings, and when you die you will be resurrected after your death, and you will have gardens better than the gardens of Jordan. And if you oppose him, there will be slaughter for you, and then you will be resurrected after your death, and there will be a fire for you in which you will be tormented." At that moment the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came out to them, holding a handful of dust, and God had blinded their eyes to him. He began to scatter it over their heads while reciting: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an﴾, until he reached His words: ﴿And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see﴾. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) then went off to attend to his need, and they stayed watching at his door. Then a man came out of the house to them after that and said: "What is wrong with you?" They said: "We are waiting for Muhammad." He said: "He has already come out to you." Not one man among them remained without having dust placed on his head. Then he went off to his need, and each one of them began to shake off the dust from his head. He said: The words of Abu Jahl reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "I too say that: for them there is slaughter from me, and he is one of them."

As for His words: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, that is: God has sealed them with misguidance, so warning does not benefit them, and they are not affected by it.

Its like has already been mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, at the commentary on the sixth verse. And as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, and even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97].

﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder﴾, that is: only the believers who follow the Reminder, which is the Great Qur'an, benefit from your warning. ﴿And fears the Most Merciful﴾, that is: in a place where no one sees him except God, he knows that God is watching over him and is aware of what he does. ﴿So give him good news of forgiveness﴾, that is: for his sins, ﴿and a noble reward﴾, that is: a great, abundant, good, and beautiful reward, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk 12].

Then God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life﴾, that is: on the Day of Resurrection. This also contains an indication that God, the Exalted, gives life to the hearts of whichever disbelievers He wills, whose hearts have died through misguidance, and then guides them to the truth, as He, the Exalted, said after mentioning the hardness of hearts: ﴿Know that God gives life to the earth after its death. We have made the signs clear to you, so that you may understand﴾ [al-Hadid 17].

He mentioned only the shackle on the neck and did not mention the hands, although the hands are intended, just as the poet said [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (22/98).]]:

*I do not know, when I set out for a land seeking good, which of the two will come upon me:*
*Is it the good that I seek, or the evil that does not leave me alone?*

He mentioned the good and left out the evil, since the context and the speech indicate it. Likewise here, since the shackle is only recognized as binding the hands together with the neck, He mentioned the neck and left out the hands.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they reach up to the chins, so they are *muqmahun*﴾. He said: This is like God's saying: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ [al-Isra' 29]. He means by this that their hands are bound to their necks, so they cannot extend them toward goodness.

Mujahid said: ﴿so they are *muqmahun*﴾: they are raising their heads, and their hands are placed over their mouths, so they are shackled from every good.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier﴾. Mujahid said: a barrier against the truth. ﴿And behind them a barrier﴾, Mujahid said: against the truth, so they wander about aimlessly. Qatadah said: a barrier against misguidance.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So We covered them﴾, that is, We covered their sight from the truth. ﴿So they do not see﴾, that is, they do not benefit from any good and are not guided to it.

Ibn Jarir said: It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to read: "*fa-a'shaynahum*" with the unpointed letter 'ayn, from *al-'asha*, which is a disease of the eye.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: God placed this barrier between them and Islam and faith, so they cannot reach it. He recited: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97]. Then he said: Whom God prevents, no one can guide.

'Ikrimah said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad, I will certainly do such-and-such to him," so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks﴾ up to His words ﴿[so] they do not see﴾. He said: They used to say: "This is Muhammad," and then they would say: "Where is he? Where is he?" They could not see him. Related by Ibn Jarir.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ziyad narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Abu Jahl said while they were sitting: "Muhammad claims that if you follow him you will become kings, and when you die you will be resurrected after your death, and you will have gardens better than the gardens of Jordan. And if you oppose him, there will be slaughter for you, and then you will be resurrected after your death, and there will be a fire for you in which you will be tormented." At that moment the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came out to them, holding a handful of dust, and God had blinded their eyes to him. He began to scatter it over their heads while reciting: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an﴾, until he reached His words: ﴿And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see﴾. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) then went off to attend to his need, and they stayed watching at his door. Then a man came out of the house to them after that and said: "What is wrong with you?" They said: "We are waiting for Muhammad." He said: "He has already come out to you." Not one man among them remained without having dust placed on his head. Then he went off to his need, and each one of them began to shake off the dust from his head. He said: The words of Abu Jahl reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "I too say that: for them there is slaughter from me, and he is one of them."

* *

As for His words: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, that is: God has sealed them with misguidance, so warning does not benefit them, and they are not affected by it.

Its like has already been mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, at the commentary on the sixth verse. And as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, and even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97].

﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder﴾, that is: only the believers who follow the Reminder, which is the Great Qur'an, benefit from your warning. ﴿And fears the Most Merciful﴾, that is: in a place where no one sees him except God, he knows that God is watching over him and is aware of what he does. ﴿So give him good news of forgiveness﴾, that is: for his sins, ﴿and a noble reward﴾, that is: a great, abundant, good, and beautiful reward, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk 12].

Then God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life﴾, that is: on the Day of Resurrection. This also contains an indication that God, the Exalted, gives life to the hearts of whichever disbelievers He wills, whose hearts have died through misguidance, and then guides them to the truth, as He, the Exalted, said after mentioning the hardness of hearts: ﴿Know that God gives life to the earth after its death. We have made the signs clear to you, so that you may understand﴾ [al-Hadid 17].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward﴾, that is: of deeds.

Regarding His words: ﴿and their traces﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: We record their deeds which they performed themselves, and their traces which they left after them, and We will recompense them for those as well, whether good or evil, as in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam, he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it after him, without any reduction from their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, he will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it after him, without any reduction from their burdens."

Related by Muslim, through the narration of Shu'bah, from 'Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, may God be pleased with him, and in it is the story of the people in woolen cloaks from Mudar [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1017.]]. Ibn Abi Hatim related it from his father, from Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Ju'fi, from Abu al-Muhayyat Yahya ibn Ya'la, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, and he mentioned the hadith in full, then recited this verse: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾.

Muslim also related it through the narration of Abu 'Awanah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father, and mentioned it [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1017.]]. Likewise is the other hadith in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him" [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1631.]].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard Mujahid say concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾: "What they left behind of misguidance."

Ibn Lahi'ah said, from 'Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾: he means what they left as a legacy. He says: What they established of a practice, which a people then acted upon after their death. If it was good, then he has the like of their rewards, without any reduction from the reward of the one who did it. And if it was evil, then upon him is the like of their burdens, without any reduction from the burden of the one who did it. Related by Ibn Abi Hatim, both of these.

This second view is the one chosen by al-Baghawi [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (7/9).]].

The second view: that what is meant by this is the traces of their steps toward obedience or disobedience.

Ibn Abi Najih and others said, from Mujahid: ﴿What they sent forward﴾: their deeds. ﴿And their traces﴾: he said: their steps with their feet. Likewise al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿And their traces﴾ means their steps. Qatadah said: If God, the Exalted, were to neglect anything of your affairs, O son of Adam, He would neglect what the winds erase of these traces. But He has counted for the son of Adam his trace and all his deeds, to the extent that He has counted even this trace in what is obedience to God or disobedience to Him. So whoever among you is able to record his trace in obedience to God, let him do so.

Several hadiths have been related with this meaning:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The areas around the mosque became empty, so the Banu Salamah wanted to move close to the mosque. This reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said to them: "It has reached me that you intend to move close to the mosque." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, we have intended that." He said: "O Banu Salamah, stay in your homes, your traces will be recorded; stay in your homes, your traces will be recorded."

Muslim related it likewise, through the hadith of Sa'id al-Juraydi and Kahmas ibn al-Hasan, both from Abu Nadrah, whose name is al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qut'ah al-'Abdi, from Jabir [[Musnad Ahmad (3/332) and Sahih Muslim, no. 665.]].

The second hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Wasiti narrated to us, Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Sufyan, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Banu Salamah were in a part of Madinah, and they wanted to move to a place near the mosque, so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Indeed, your traces are being recorded." So they did not move.

Al-Tirmidhi alone related it, in the commentary on this noble verse, from Muhammad ibn al-Wazir, with this chain. Then he said: "Hasan gharib, from the hadith of al-Thawri" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3226.]].

Ibn Jarir related it from Sulayman ibn 'Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Tarif, who is Ibn Shihab Abu Sufyan al-Sa'di, from Abu Nadrah, with this [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/100).]].

It has also been related by a route other than al-Thawri. The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said:

'Abbad ibn Ziyad al-Saji narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Juraydi, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id who said: The Banu Salamah complained to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the distance of their homes from the mosque, so this was revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾, and they remained in their place.

Ibn al-Muthanna also narrated to us: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

In it there is strangeness regarding the mention of the revelation of this verse, while the surah in its entirety is Meccan, and God knows best.

The third hadith: Ibn Jarir said:

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 36, verses 8–12 (part 2 of 2)**

Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Jahḍamī narrated to us: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The dwellings of the Anṣār were far from the mosque, so they wanted to move closer to the mosque. Then this was revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾. So they said: "We will remain in our places." Thus he narrated it, and there is nothing in it that is *marfūʿ* (traced back to the Prophet ﷺ). [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/100).]

Al-Ṭabarānī also narrated it, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam, from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Firyābī, from Isrāʾīl, from Simāk, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Anṣār's dwellings were far from the mosque, so they wanted to relocate closer to the mosque. Then this was revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾, so they remained in their dwellings. [Al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (12/8). Its narrator ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam is weak.]

**The fourth hadith:** Imam Aḥmad said: Ḥasan narrated to us: Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us: Ḥayy ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: A man died in Medina, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed over him and said: "Would that he had died somewhere other than his birthplace!" A man among the people said: "And why, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When a man dies outside his birthplace, a measure of his birthplace is allotted to him in Paradise, up to the place where his traces end."

Al-Nasāʾī narrated it from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, and Ibn Mājah from Ḥarmalah, both from Ibn Wahb, from Ḥayy ibn ʿAbd Allāh, with the same wording. [Al-Musnad (2/177), Sunan al-Nasāʾī (4/7), and Sunan Ibn Mājah, no. 1614.]

Ibn Jarīr (al-Ṭabarī) also said: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us: Abū Tumaylah narrated to us: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, from Thābit, who said: I walked with Anas and quickened my pace, so he took my hand and we walked slowly. When we finished the prayer, Anas said: I walked with Zayd ibn Thābit and quickened my pace, and he said: "O Anas, did you not realise that traces are recorded? Did you not realise that traces are recorded?" [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/100).]

This statement does not contradict the first one. Rather, it draws attention to the same meaning by way of an even stronger and more fitting inference. For if these traces are recorded, then the deeds that set an example for others, whether good or evil, are all the more deserving of being recorded. And Allah knows best.

\* \*

As for His saying: ﴿And We have enumerated all things in a clear register﴾, meaning: all created things are written in a manifest book, preserved in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ*). The "clear register" (*al-Imām al-Mubīn*) here is the Mother of the Book (*Umm al-Kitāb*). This is the view of Mujāhid, Qatādah, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. The same applies to His saying: ﴿On the day We shall call every people with their record﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 71], meaning: with the book of their deeds, which bears witness against them for the good and evil they did. As Allah says: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward﴾ [al-Zumar: 69], and He says: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say: "Woe to us! What kind of book is this? It leaves out nothing small or great but has recorded it all." And they will find what they did present there, and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

The Lord, exalted is He, says: Present to your people, O Muhammad, those who denied you, an example: the companions of the town, when the messengers came to it.

Ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of what reached him from Ibn Abbas, Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Wahb ibn Munabbih: "It is the city of Antioch (Antakiya). Its king was called Antiykhus ibn Antiykhus ibn Antiykhus, and he worshipped idols. God sent to him three messengers, and they were Sadiq, Sadquq, and Shalum [[In manuscript T: "Shakum."]], and he denied them."

It was similarly narrated from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and al-Zuhri that it is Antioch.

Some of the imams (a'imma) found the identification of it as Antioch problematic, for a reason we will mention after completing the story, God willing.

* *

His saying: ﴿When We sent to them two, and they denied them both﴾ means they rushed to deny them. ﴿Then We strengthened them with a third﴾ means We reinforced them and strengthened their support with a third messenger.

Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Wahb ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i, who said: "The names of the first two messengers were Shim'un and Yuhanna, the name of the third was Bulus, and the town was Antioch."

﴿They said﴾ means, to the people of that town: ﴿Indeed, we are sent to you﴾ means from your Lord, who created you, commanding you to worship Him alone, with no partner. This was said by Abu al-Aliyah.

Qatadah ibn Di'amah claimed that they were messengers of the Messiah, upon him be peace, to the people of Antioch. ﴿They said, "You are not but human beings like us"﴾ means: how can revelation be sent to you when you are human and we are human? Why, then, would revelation not be sent to us like you? And if you were messengers, you would be angels. This is similar to what many disbelieving nations said, as God, exalted is He, related about them in His saying: ﴿That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?"﴾ [At-Taghabun: 6], so they were astonished by that and denied it. And His saying: ﴿They said, "You are not but human beings like us. You want to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship, so bring us a clear authority"﴾ [Ibrahim: 10]. And His saying, relating their words: ﴿And if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers﴾ [Al-Muminun: 34], and ﴿Nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has God sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [Al-Isra: 94]. For this reason these said: ﴿You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing. You are not but liars.﴾ ﴿They said, "Our Lord knows that we are indeed sent to you."﴾ That is, the three messengers answered them, saying: God knows that we are His messengers to you. Had we lied about Him, He would have punished us with the most severe punishment. But He will honour us and grant us victory over you, and you will come to know whose will be the final outcome of the abode, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "God is sufficient as a witness between me and you. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in God, those are the losers."﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 52] [[In manuscripts T, S, A, and H: "He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth," and the correct reading is what we have adopted.]]

﴿And upon us is only the clear conveyance﴾ means: they are saying, "Our duty is only to convey to you what we have been sent with. If you obey, you will have happiness in this world and the next. And if you do not respond, you will come to know the consequence of that." And God knows best.

The Lord, exalted is He, says: Present to your people, O Muhammad, those who denied you, an example: the companions of the town, when the messengers came to it.

It was similarly narrated from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and al-Zuhri that it is Antioch.

Some of the imams (a'imma) found the identification of it as Antioch problematic, for a reason we will mention after completing the story, God willing.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 36, verse 18–19:

Then the people of the town said to them: ﴿Indeed, we consider you a bad omen.﴾ That is, we have not seen anything good in your faces in our livelihood.

Qatadah said: They say, "If evil befalls us, it is only because of you."

Mujahid said: They say, "No one like you has entered a town except that its people were punished."

﴿If you do not desist, we will surely stone you,﴾ Qatadah said: "with stones." Mujahid said: "with abuse."

﴿And a painful punishment will surely touch you from us.﴾ That is, a severe punishment.

Then their messengers said: ﴿Your omen is with you﴾ — that is, it will return upon you. This is like the statement of Allah the Exalted about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours," and if evil afflicted them, they ascribed it to Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their omen is with Allah﴾ [Al-A'raf: 131]. And the people of Salih said: [[In (manuscripts) T and S: "Lut" and in (manuscript) A: "Shu'ayb".]] ﴿We consider you and those with you a bad omen. He said, "Your omen is with Allah"﴾ [An-Naml: 47]. Qatadah and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: That is, your deeds are with you. Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," and if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾ [An-Nisa': 78].

* *

As for His statement: ﴿Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people.﴾ That is: because we reminded you and commanded you to affirm the Oneness of Allah and to sincerely devote worship to Him, you met us with this speech, and threatened and intimidated us? Rather, you are a transgressing people.

Qatadah said: That is, if we remind you of Allah, you consider us a bad omen. Rather, you are a transgressing people.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah Ya-Sin (36), verses 20–25:

Ibn Ishaq said, on what reached him from Ibn 'Abbas, Ka'b al-Ahbar and Wahb ibn Munabbih: The people of the town resolved to kill their messengers, and a man came from the farthest part of the city, running (*yas'a*), that is, to support them against their people. They said: he was Habib, and he used to make *al-jarir*, which is ropes [in T, S, A: "yu'nā", meaning "that is"]. He was a sick man whom leprosy (*al-judham*) had afflicted severely, and he was abundant in charity, giving away half of his earnings, and his outlook was upright [in A: "al-fitrah", meaning "natural disposition"].

Ibn Ishaq also said, from a man he named, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, or from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The name of the companion of Ya-Sin was Habib, and leprosy had spread through him.

al-Thawri said, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu Majlaz: His name was Habib ibn Mara.

Shabib ibn Bishr [in A: "Bashir"] said, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas [also]: The name of the companion of Ya-Sin was Habib al-Najjar (the carpenter), and his people killed him.

al-Suddi said: He was a launderer (*qassar*). 'Umar ibn al-Hakam said: He was a cobbler (*iskafi*). Qatadah said: He used to worship in a cave there.

Allah says: ﴿O my people, follow the messengers.﴾ He urges his people to follow the messengers who came to them. ﴿Follow those who ask you no reward﴾, that is, for conveying the message. ﴿And they are rightly guided﴾ in what they call you to, of worshipping Allah alone, with no partner.

﴿And why should I not worship He who created me﴾, that is: what prevents me from sincerely worshipping the One who created me, alone with no partner? ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾, that is, on the Day of Return, when He will recompense you for your deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

﴿Shall I take besides Him gods?﴾ This is a question of denial, rebuke and reproach. ﴿If the Most Merciful intends for me some harm, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me.﴾ That is: these gods you worship besides Him possess nothing of the matter. For if Allah wills harm for me, ﴿none can remove it but He﴾ [Yunus 10:107], and these idols cannot repel or prevent that, nor can they save me from what I am in. ﴿Indeed I would then be in clear error﴾, that is, if I took them as gods besides Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so hear me﴾: Ibn Ishaq said, on what reached him from Ibn 'Abbas, Ka'b and Wahb: He says to his people: ﴿Indeed, I have believed in your Lord﴾, whom you have disbelieved in, ﴿so hear me﴾, that is, listen to my words.

It is also possible that his address, with his words ﴿Indeed, I have believed in your Lord﴾, was to the messengers, meaning the One who sent you, ﴿so hear me﴾, that is, bear witness for me to that before Him. Ibn Jarir related this, saying: Others said: rather, he addressed the messengers with that and said to them: Listen to my words, so that you may bear witness for me before my Lord to what I say to you: indeed I have believed in your Lord and followed you. [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/104).]

And this view which these scholars related is more apparent in meaning, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Ishaq said, on what reached him from Ibn 'Abbas, Ka'b and Wahb: So when he said that, they leapt upon him as one man and killed him, and there was no one to defend him.

Qatadah said: They began stoning him, while he was saying: "O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know." They did not cease to attack him until they struck him down while he was still saying that, and so they killed him, may Allah have mercy on him.

He was a sick man whom leprosy (*al-judham*) had afflicted severely, and he was abundant in charity, giving away half of his earnings, and his outlook was upright [in A: "al-fitrah", meaning "natural disposition"].

Ibn Ishaq also said, from a man he named, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, or from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The name of the companion of Ya-Sin was Habib, and leprosy had spread through him.

al-Thawri said, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu Majlaz: His name was Habib ibn Mara.

Shabib ibn Bishr [in A: "Bashir"] said, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas [also]: The name of the companion of Ya-Sin was Habib al-Najjar (the carpenter), and his people killed him.

al-Suddi said: He was a launderer (*qassar*). 'Umar ibn al-Hakam said: He was a cobbler (*iskafi*). Qatadah said: He used to worship in a cave there.

Allah says: ﴿O my people, follow the messengers.﴾ He urges his people to follow the messengers who came to them. ﴿Follow those who ask you no reward﴾, that is, for conveying the message. ﴿And they are rightly guided﴾ in what they call you to, of worshipping Allah alone, with no partner.

﴿And why should I not worship He who created me﴾, that is: what prevents me from sincerely worshipping the One who created me, alone with no partner? ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾, that is, on the Day of Return, when He will recompense you for your deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

﴿Shall I take besides Him gods?﴾ This is a question of denial, rebuke and reproach. ﴿If the Most Merciful intends for me some harm, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me.﴾ That is: these gods you worship besides Him possess nothing of the matter. For if Allah wills harm for me, ﴿none can remove it but He﴾ [Yunus 10:107], and these idols cannot repel or prevent that, nor can they save me from what I am in. ﴿Indeed I would then be in clear error﴾, that is, if I took them as gods besides Allah.

* *

It is also possible that his address, with his words ﴿Indeed, I have believed in your Lord﴾, was to the messengers, meaning the One who sent you, ﴿so hear me﴾, that is, bear witness for me to that before Him. And this view which these scholars related is more apparent in meaning, and Allah knows best.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I fear that they will kill you." He said: "If they find me sleeping, they will not wake me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Go." Allah also states that He did not send down upon them, and in destroying them He did not need to send down an army of angels against them; rather, the matter was far easier than that. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, as narrated by Ibn Ishaq from some of his companions, from him, that he said regarding His saying: ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We ever going to send down [any host]﴾, meaning: We did not need to overpower them with multitudes; the matter was easier for Us than that. ﴿It was but one cry, and at once they were extinguished﴾. He said: So Allah destroyed that king and destroyed the people of Antioch, and they were wiped off the face of the earth, and not a single survivor of them remained.

It was also said: ﴿nor were We ever going to send down [any host]﴾ means: We would not send the angels down upon the nations when We destroy them; rather, We send upon them a punishment that annihilates them.

It was also said: the meaning of His saying ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven﴾ is: no other message was sent to them. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. It has already been mentioned from many of the early generations (salaf) that this town is Antioch, and that these three were messengers from the Messiah, peace be upon him, as Qatadah and others stated explicitly. This is the view which is not attributed to any one of the later exegetes (mufassirun) other than him, and there is scrutiny of it from several aspects:

The first: the apparent sense of the story indicates that these were messengers of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not from the side of the Messiah, as He said: ﴿When We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened [them] with a third, and they said: "Indeed, we are messengers to you."﴾ until they said: ﴿"Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you. And Allah knows best.

He said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from some of his companions, from Ibn Mas'ud: "They trampled him with their feet until his intestines came out through his anus. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: my father related to us, Hisham ibn Ubaydullah related to us, Ibn Jabir, namely Muhammad, related to us, from Abd al-Malik, namely Ibn Umayr, who said: Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Send me to my people to call them to Islam." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I fear that they will kill you." He said: "If they find me sleeping, they will not wake me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Go." So he set off and passed by al-Lat and al-Uzza, and said: "I will surely greet you tomorrow with what will displease you." Thaqif became angry. He said: "O people of Thaqif, al-Lat is not a lord, and al-Uzza is not a lord. Embrace Islam and you will be safe." He said: "O assembly of the Ahlaf, al-Uzza is not a lord, and al-Lat is not a lord. Al-Tabarani also narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/148) through Musa ibn Uqbah, from al-Zuhri, in similar wording. When [Musaylimah] began asking him about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he kept saying: "Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" He would say: "Yes." Then [Musaylimah] would say: "Do you testify that I am a messenger of Allah?" He would say: "I do not hear." Musaylimah would say to him: "Do you hear this but not that?" He would say: "Yes." So [Musaylimah] began cutting him limb by limb, and each time he asked him, [Habib] did not add anything to that answer, until he died in his hands. When it was said to Ka'b, he said: "His name is Habib, and by Allah, the companion of Ya-Sin was named Habib." [Note: Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (22/103).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We ever going to send down [any host]﴾: Allah informs that He took vengeance upon his people after they killed him, out of His anger against them, because they denied His messengers and killed His friend. Allah also states that He did not send down upon them, and in destroying them He did not need to send down an army of angels against them; rather, the matter was far easier than that. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, as narrated by Ibn Ishaq from some of his companions, from him, that he said regarding His saying: ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We ever going to send down [any host]﴾, meaning: We did not need to overpower them with multitudes; the matter was easier for Us than that. ﴿It was but one cry, and at once they were extinguished﴾. He said: So Allah destroyed that king and destroyed the people of Antioch, and they were wiped off the face of the earth, and not a single survivor of them remained.

It was also said: ﴿nor were We ever going to send down [any host]﴾ means: We would not send the angels down upon the nations when We destroy them; rather, We send upon them a punishment that annihilates them.

It was also said: the meaning of His saying ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven﴾ is: no other message was sent to them. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. It has already been mentioned from many of the early generations (salaf) that this town is Antioch, and that these three were messengers from the Messiah, peace be upon him, as Qatadah and others stated explicitly. This is the view which is not attributed to any one of the later exegetes (mufassirun) other than him, and there is scrutiny of it from several aspects:

The first: the apparent sense of the story indicates that these were messengers of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not from the side of the Messiah, as He said: ﴿When We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened [them] with a third, and they said: "Indeed, we are messengers to you."﴾ until they said: ﴿"Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you. Had these been disciples (hawariyyun), they would have used a phrase suitable to their being from the Messiah, peace be upon him; and Allah knows best. Moreover, if they had been messengers of the Messiah, they would not have said to them: ﴿"You are only human beings like us."﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:15].

The second: the people of Antioch believed in the messengers of the Messiah sent to them, and it was the first city to believe in the Messiah. For this reason, among the Christians it was one of the four cities in which there is a patriarchate (bataraka), namely: Jerusalem, because it is the city of the Messiah; Antioch, because it was the first town to believe in the Messiah, from its last people; and Alexandria, because in it they agreed on establishing patriarchs, metropolitans, bishops, priests, deacons and monks. Then Rome, because it is the city of King Constantine, who supported their religion and strengthened it. When he built Constantinople, they moved the patriarch from Rome to it, as mentioned by more than one who recorded their histories, such as Sa'id ibn Bitriq and others from among the People of the Book and the Muslims. Thus, once it is established that Antioch was the first city to believe, the people of this town are those whom Allah, the Exalted, mentioned as having denied His messengers, and that He destroyed them with one cry that extinguished them. And Allah knows best.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and more than one of the early generations mentioned that after sending down the Torah, Allah, the Exalted, did not destroy any nation entirely with a punishment sent upon them; rather, He commanded the believers after that to fight the polytheists. They mentioned this in connection with His saying: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the Book after We had destroyed the former generations﴾ [Al-Qasas 28:43]. Based on this, it is necessary that the town mentioned in the Qur'an [the Great] is another town other than Antioch, as more than one of the early generations also stated explicitly. Or, if the word "Antioch" is preserved in this story, it refers to another city besides this well-known, famous one, for this one is not known to have been destroyed, neither in the Christian religion nor before it. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 36, verse 30–32:

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Alas for the servants!﴾ He said: meaning, "Woe to the servants!"

Qatadah said: ﴿Alas for the servants!﴾ meaning: "Alas for the servants themselves, over what they squandered of Allah's command, what they neglected in regard to Allah." He said: "And in some recitations: 'Alas for the servants [[In T, S, A: "Alas for"]] themselves.'"

The meaning of this is: their regret and remorse on the Day of Resurrection, when they witness the punishment, how they denied the messengers of Allah and opposed the command of Allah. For they, in the worldly abode, were the deniers among them.

﴿No messenger came to them but that they used to mock him.﴾ That is: they denied him, mocked him, and rejected the truth with which he was sent.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they do not return to them?﴾ That is: have they not taken warning from those whom Allah destroyed before them among the deniers of the messengers, how there was no return or recurrence for them to this worldly life? And the matter is not as many of their ignorant and wicked ones claimed, saying: ﴿There is nothing but our worldly life; we die and we live﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 37]. They are the ones among the Dahriyyah who speak of recurrence (al-dawr), and they are those who, out of their ignorance, believe that they will return to the world as they were in it. So Allah, the Exalted, refuted their falsehood, saying: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they do not return to them?﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, all of them will be brought before Us, presented.﴾ That is: all of the past and future nations will be brought forth for reckoning on the Day of Resurrection before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He will recompense them for all their deeds, good and bad. The meaning of this is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, your Lord will fully repay them for their deeds﴾ [Hud: 111].

The reciters differed in the pronunciation of this particle. Some of them read "wa-in kullun lamma" with lightening (takhfif), so in their view "in" is affirmative. Others stressed "lamma" and made "in" negating, with "lamma" meaning "illa" (except), its implied sense being: "And there is none but that they are all brought before Us, presented." The meaning of both readings is one, and Allah knows best.
