They are the ones among the Dahriyyah who speak of recurrence (al-dawr), and they are those who, out of their ignorance, believe that they will return to the world as they were in it. So Allah, the Exalted, refuted their falsehood, saying: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they do not return to them?﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, all of them will be brought before Us, presented.﴾ That is: all of the past and future nations will be brought forth for reckoning on the Day of Resurrection before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He will recompense them for all their deeds, good and bad. The meaning of this is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, your Lord will fully repay them for their deeds﴾ [Hud: 111].

The reciters differed in the pronunciation of this particle. Some of them read "wa-in kullun lamma" with lightening (takhfif), so in their view "in" is affirmative. Others stressed "lamma" and made "in" negating, with "lamma" meaning "illa" (except), its implied sense being: "And there is none but that they are all brought before Us, presented." The meaning of both readings is one, and Allah knows best.

**Ibn Kathir's Commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah Ya-Sin, verses 33–36:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And a sign for them﴾, i.e., a proof for them of the existence of the Creator, His complete power, and His giving life to the dead. ﴿is the dead earth﴾, i.e., when it is dead and lifeless, with no vegetation in it. But when Allah sends down water upon it, it stirs and swells, and it produces every beautiful kind of growth. Therefore He said: ﴿We have revived it and brought forth from it grain, of which they eat﴾, i.e., We made it a provision for them and for their livestock. ﴿And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and We caused to gush forth therein some of the springs﴾, i.e., We placed in it rivers flowing through places where they need them, so that they may eat of its fruit. When He bestowed favour upon His creatures by bringing forth crops for them, He followed it with mention of fruits, their variety and their kinds.

* *

His saying: ﴿and their hands did not make it﴾, i.e., all of that is only from Allah's mercy toward them, not by their effort or toil, nor by their own strength and power. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah. Therefore He said: ﴿Will they not then be grateful?﴾, i.e., will they not thank Him for these blessings He has bestowed upon them, which cannot be counted or enumerated?

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) preferred, indeed affirmed, that the "mā" in His saying ﴿and their hands did not make it﴾ means "that which" (alladhī), its meaning being: "that they may eat of its fruit and of that which their hands made," i.e., they planted it and set it up. He said: it is also so in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿that they may eat of its fruit and that which their hands made. Will they not then be grateful?﴾

Then He said: ﴿Glorified is He who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾, i.e., of crops, fruits and plants, ﴿and of themselves﴾, by making them male and female, ﴿and of what they do not know﴾, i.e., of various creatures they do not recognize, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And of everything We created pairs, that you may remember﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 49].

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (1954), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1100), from the hadith of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾. Regarding His saying ﴿to a resting place for it﴾ there are two views.

The first: the intended meaning is its place of rest in space, which is beneath the Throne ('Arsh) on the side that faces the earth. Wherever the sun is, it is beneath the Throne, and all creatures are beneath it, since it is their ceiling. It is not a sphere, as many of the astronomers (ahl al-hay'a, the people of celestial science) claim; rather it is a dome with legs, carried by the angels, and it is above the world on the side facing the heads of people. So when the sun is at the zenith of the sky at midday, it is at its closest to the Throne. When it has turned in its fourth orbit to the opposite position of this place, which is the time of midnight, it becomes at its farthest from the Throne. At that time it prostrates and asks permission to rise, as the hadiths have reported.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim [al-Taymi], [[Addition from manuscripts T, S, A.]] from his father, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in the mosque at sunset, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, do you know where the sun sets?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It goes on until it prostrates beneath the Throne. That is His saying: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾."

Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about His saying: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it﴾, and he said: "Its resting place is beneath the Throne." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4802, 4803).]]

This is how he narrated it here. It was also related by him in several places [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (3199, 7424, 7433).]], and the rest of the group (the authors of the six books), except Ibn Majah, related it by several chains from al-A'mash, with the same wording. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (159); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4002); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3227); and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11430).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the mosque when the sun set, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, do you know where the sun goes?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It goes on until it prostrates before its Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and then it asks permission to return, and permission is granted. It is as if it is told: Return from where you came. So it returns to its rising place, and that is its resting place." Then he recited: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it﴾. [[Al-Musnad (5/152).]]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Dharr when the sun had set: "Do you know where this is?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It goes on until it prostrates beneath the Throne, and it asks permission, and permission is granted to it. Soon it will prostrate and it will not be accepted from it, and it will ask permission and it will not be granted to it, and it will be told: Return from where you came." So it rises from its west, and that is His saying: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾. [[In manuscript T: "wa-as'alana" (and we asked).]]

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Wahb ibn Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said regarding His saying: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it﴾: The sun rises, and the sins of the children of Adam turn it back, until when it sets it gives greetings and prostrates and asks permission, and permission is granted to it. Then one day it sets, gives greetings, prostrates and asks permission, but permission is not granted to it. It says: The journey is far, and if I am not permitted I will not reach it. So it is detained for as long as Allah wills to detain it. Then it is told: "Rise from where you set." He said: "From that day until the Day of Resurrection, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith." [[Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (2/115). Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. (628), through the chain of Abd al-Razzaq.]]

It was also said: the intended meaning of ﴿to a resting place for it﴾ is the end of its course, and that is the limit of its height in the sky in summer, which is its apogee (awj), and then the limit of its descent in winter, which is its perigee (hadid).

The second view: the intended meaning of its resting place is the end of its course, which is the Day of Resurrection. Its motion will cease, its movement will become still, and it will be folded up, and this world will come to its end. This is its temporal resting place.

Qatadah said: ﴿to a resting place for it﴾ means: to its appointed time, and to a term it will not exceed.

It was also said: the intended meaning is that it continues to move through its summer risings for a period it will not exceed. This is narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr.

Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas recited: "And the sun runs, there is no resting place for it" [Arabic: lā mustaqarra lahā]. That is: it has no settling place and no stillness. Rather it travels night and day, neither slackening nor stopping. As He said: ﴿And He subjected to you the sun and the moon, both continuously﴾ [Ibrahim: 33], that is, they neither slacken nor stop until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty﴾, that is, the One whom none can oppose or resist, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of all movements and stillnesses. He has determined that and fixed it in a pattern with no variation or reversal, as He said: ﴿The Splitter of the dawn, and He made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Al-An'am: 96]. In the same way He concluded the verse of Ha Mim al-Sajdah with His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 12]. [[In manuscript T: "concluded the last verse."]] Then He said: ﴿And for the moon We have determined stations﴾, that is, We made it travel a different course by which one can know the passing of the months, just as by the sun the night and day are known. As He said: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: They are timings for people and for the Hajj﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 189]. He also said: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined its stations so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ [Yunus: 5], and He said: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs. We obliterated the sign of the night and made the sign of the day to give sight, that you may seek bounty from your Lord and that you may know the number of years and the reckoning. And everything We have explained in detail﴾ [Al-Isra': 12]. So He made the sun to have a light specific to it, and the moon [[In manuscript S: "wa-li-l-qamar" (and for the moon).]] to have a light specific to it, and He differentiated between the movement of this and that. The sun rises every day and sets at its end with one kind of light, but it moves in its risings and settings in summer and winter. Because of this the day lengthens and the night shortens, then the night lengthens and the day shortens. He made its authority in the day, so it is a daytime luminary. As for the moon, He determined its stations: it rises on the first night of the month small and faintly lit, then on the second night it gains light and rises a station, and as it rises it increases in brightness, though its light is borrowed from the sun, until its light is complete on the fourteenth night. Then it begins to wane until the end of the month, until it becomes like the old date-stalk [Arabic: ka-l-'urjun al-qadim].

Ibn Abbas said: It is the base of the cluster (al-'idhq).

Mujahid said: The old date-stalk (al-'urjun al-qadim) is the dry cluster (al-'idhq al-yabis).

Ibn Abbas meant: the base of the cluster of dates when it has ripened, dried and bent, and others said likewise. Then after this, Allah brings it forth anew at the start of the next month. The Arabs named each group of three nights of the month according to the moon's phases. They called the first three "ghurar" (bright ones), the next "nufal," the ones after them "tusa'" (ninths), because the last of them is the ninth, and the ones after them "'ushar" (tenths), because the first of them is the tenth. The ones after them they called "al-bid" (the white ones), because the moon's light remains in them to their end. The ones after them they called "dura'" (plural of dar'a', dark-headed), because the first of them is dark, due to the late rising of the moon in them, and from this comes the phrase "al-shatu al-dar'a'," meaning a goat whose head is black. After them are three called "zulam" (dark ones), then three called "hanadis" (very dark ones), then three called "da'a'id," and three called "mihaq" (waning ones), because the moon wanes into nothing at the end of the month in them. Abu Ubayd [[In manuscript A: "Abu Ubaydah."]] used to deny the names "tusa'" and "'ushar." So he said in his book Gharib al-Musannaf.

* *

His saying: ﴿Nor is it for the sun to overtake the moon﴾. Mujahid said: each of them has a limit it does not exceed and does not fall short of. When the authority of this one comes, the other departs, and when the authority of this one departs, the authority of that one comes.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿Nor is it for the sun to overtake the moon﴾, he said: That refers to the night of the crescent.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak that he said: The wind has wings, and the moon takes refuge in a sheath of water.

al-Thawri said, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih: This does not overtake the light of that, nor does that overtake the light of this. [[In manuscript S: "does not overtake the harm of that, nor that the harm of this."]] Ikrimah said regarding His saying ﴿Nor is it for the sun to overtake the moon﴾ [[Addition from manuscript A.]]: meaning that each of them has its own authority, so it is not fitting for the sun to rise at night.

* *

His saying: ﴿Nor does the night outstrip the day﴾. It means: it is not fitting that when night comes there should be another night until the day comes, since the authority of the sun is by day and the authority of the moon is by night.

al-Dahhak said: The night does not depart from here until the day comes from here, and he gestured with his hand toward the east.

Mujahid said: ﴿Nor does the night outstrip the day﴾: they pursue each other swiftly, one stripping away from the other.

The meaning of this is: there is no interval between night and day. Rather each follows the other without delay or gap, because they are subjected and continuously pursue each other with swift pursuit.

* *

His saying: ﴿And each in an orbit is swimming﴾. That is: the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, all of them are swimming, that is, they revolve in the orbit of the sky. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ata al-Khurasani. [[In manuscript T: "Said by Ibn Abbas and others."]]

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "In a falak (orbit) between the heaven and the earth." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, and it is very strange (gharib jiddan), indeed munkar (rejected).

Ibn Abbas and others among the early generations (al-salaf) said: "In a falakah like the falakah of the spindle (mighzal)."

Mujahid said: "The falak is like the iron of the millstone (al-rahá), or like the falakah of the spindle, the spindle does not turn except by it, nor does it turn except by the spindle."

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Dharr when the sun had set: "Do you know where this is?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It goes on until it prostrates beneath the Throne, and it asks permission, and permission is granted to it. Soon it will prostrate and it will not be accepted from it, and it will ask permission and it will not be granted to it, and it will be told: Return from where you came." So it rises from its west, and that is His saying: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾. [[In manuscript T: "wa-as'alana" (and we asked).]]

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Wahb ibn Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said regarding His saying: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it﴾: The sun rises, and the sins of the children of Adam turn it back, until when it sets it gives greetings and prostrates and asks permission, and permission is granted to it. Then one day it sets, gives greetings, prostrates and asks permission, but permission is not granted to it. It says: The journey is far, and if I am not permitted I will not reach it. So it is detained for as long as Allah wills to detain it. Then it is told: "Rise from where you set." He said: "From that day until the Day of Resurrection, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith." [[Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (2/115). Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. (628), through the chain of Abd al-Razzaq.]]

It was also said: the intended meaning of ﴿to a resting place for it﴾ is the end of its course, and that is the limit of its height in the sky in summer, which is its apogee (awj), and then the limit of its descent in winter, which is its perigee (hadid).

The second view: the intended meaning of its resting place is the end of its course, which is the Day of Resurrection. Its motion will cease, its movement will become still, and it will be folded up, and this world will come to its end. This is its temporal resting place.

Qatadah said: ﴿to a resting place for it﴾ means: to its appointed time, and to a term it will not exceed.

It was also said: the intended meaning is that it continues to move through its summer risings for a period it will not exceed. This is narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr.

Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas recited: "And the sun runs, there is no resting place for it" [Arabic: lā mustaqarra lahā]. That is: it has no settling place and no stillness. Rather it travels night and day, neither slackening nor stopping. As He said: ﴿And He subjected to you the sun and the moon, both continuously﴾ [Ibrahim: 33], that is, they neither slacken nor stop until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty﴾, that is, the One whom none can oppose or resist, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of all movements and stillnesses. He has determined that and fixed it in a pattern with no variation or reversal, as He said: ﴿The Splitter of the dawn, and He made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Al-An'am: 96]. In the same way He concluded the verse of Ha Mim al-Sajdah with His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 12]. [[In manuscript T: "concluded the last verse."]] Then He said: ﴿And for the moon We have determined stations﴾, that is, We made it travel a different course by which one can know the passing of the months, just as by the sun the night and day are known. As He said: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: They are timings for people and for the Hajj﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 189]. He also said: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined its stations so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ [Yunus: 5], and He said: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs. We obliterated the sign of the night and made the sign of the day to give sight, that you may seek bounty from your Lord and that you may know the number of years and the reckoning. And everything We have explained in detail﴾ [Al-Isra': 12]. So He made the sun to have a light specific to it, and the moon [[In manuscript S: "wa-li-l-qamar" (and for the moon).]] to have a light specific to it, and He differentiated between the movement of this and that. The sun rises every day and sets at its end with one kind of light, but it moves in its risings and settings in summer and winter. Because of this the day lengthens and the night shortens, then the night lengthens and the day shortens. He made its authority in the day, so it is a daytime luminary. As for the moon, He determined its stations: it rises on the first night of the month small and faintly lit, then on the second night it gains light and rises a station, and as it rises it increases in brightness, though its light is borrowed from the sun, until its light is complete on the fourteenth night. Then it begins to wane until the end of the month, until it becomes like the old date-stalk [Arabic: ka-l-'urjun al-qadim].

Ibn Abbas said: It is the base of the cluster (al-'idhq).

Mujahid said: The old date-stalk (al-'urjun al-qadim) is the dry cluster (al-'idhq al-yabis).

Ibn Abbas meant: the base of the cluster of dates when it has ripened, dried and bent, and others said likewise. Then after this, Allah brings it forth anew at the start of the next month. The Arabs named each group of three nights of the month according to the moon's phases. They called the first three "ghurar" (bright ones), the next "nufal," the ones after them "tusa'" (ninths), because the last of them is the ninth, and the ones after them "'ushar" (tenths), because the first of them is the tenth. The ones after them they called "al-bid" (the white ones), because the moon's light remains in them to their end. The ones after them they called "dura'" (plural of dar'a', dark-headed), because the first of them is dark, due to the late rising of the moon in them, and from this comes the phrase "al-shatu al-dar'a'," meaning a goat whose head is black. After them are three called "zulam" (dark ones), then three called "hanadis" (very dark ones), then three called "da'a'id," and three called "mihaq" (waning ones), because the moon wanes into nothing at the end of the month in them. Abu Ubayd [[In manuscript A: "Abu Ubaydah."]] used to deny the names "tusa'" and "'ushar." So he said in his book Gharib al-Musannaf.

* *

His saying: ﴿Nor is it for the sun to overtake the moon﴾. Mujahid said: each of them has a limit it does not exceed and does not fall short of. When the authority of this one comes, the other departs, and when the authority of this one departs, the authority of that one comes.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿Nor is it for the sun to overtake the moon﴾, he said: That refers to the night of the crescent.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak that he said: The wind has wings, and the moon takes refuge in a sheath of water.

al-Thawri said, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih: This does not overtake the light of that, nor does that overtake the light of this. [[In manuscript S: "does not overtake the harm of that, nor that the harm of this."]] Ikrimah said regarding His saying ﴿Nor is it for the sun to overtake the moon﴾ [[Addition from manuscript A.]]: meaning that each of them has its own authority, so it is not fitting for the sun to rise at night.

* *

His saying: ﴿Nor does the night outstrip the day﴾. It means: it is not fitting that when night comes there should be another night until the day comes, since the authority of the sun is by day and the authority of the moon is by night.

al-Dahhak said: The night does not depart from here until the day comes from here, and he gestured with his hand toward the east.

Mujahid said: ﴿Nor does the night outstrip the day﴾: they pursue each other swiftly, one stripping away from the other.

The meaning of this is: there is no interval between night and day. Rather each follows the other without delay or gap, because they are subjected and continuously pursue each other with swift pursuit.

* *

His saying: ﴿And each in an orbit is swimming﴾. That is: the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, all of them are swimming, that is, they revolve in the orbit of the sky. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ata al-Khurasani. [[In manuscript T: "Said by Ibn Abbas and others."]]

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "In a falak (orbit) between the heaven and the earth." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, and it is very strange (gharib jiddan), indeed munkar (rejected).

Ibn Abbas and others among the early generations (al-salaf) said: "In a falakah like the falakah of the spindle (mighzal)."

Mujahid said: "The falak is like the iron of the millstone (al-rahá), or like the falakah of the spindle, the spindle does not turn except by it, nor does it turn except by the spindle."

Allah the Exalted says: And it is also a sign for them of His power: His subjecting the sea so that it carries the ships (in it). Among that, indeed its first (instance), is the ship of Nuh (Noah), peace be upon him, in which Allah saved him together with those believers who were with him, and there remained upon the face of the earth none of the offspring of Adam other than them. Therefore He said: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring﴾, i.e., their forefathers, ﴿in the laden ship﴾, i.e., in the ship filled with goods and animals, which Allah commanded him to carry in it from every kind two (of each).

Ibn 'Abbas said: al-mashhun (the laden) means al-muqar (the loaded). Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, Qatadah, [al-Dahhak] and al-Suddi.

And al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: it is the ship of Nuh, peace be upon him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We created for them of the like of it that which they ride﴾: al-Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: he meant by this the camels, for they are "the ships of the land"; they carry loads on them and ride them. Likewise said Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatadah, in a narration of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, and others.

Al-Suddi said, in one narration: it is the livestock (al-an'am).

Ibn Jarir said: al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Do you know what ﴿And We created for them of the like of it that which they ride﴾ is? We said: No. He said: It is the ships, made after the ship of Nuh, in its likeness.

Likewise said [more than one (scholar)] Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Abu Salih, and al-Suddi also: what is meant by His saying ﴿And We created for them of the like of it that which they ride﴾ is: i.e., the ships.

This view in meaning is strengthened by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose high, We carried you in the flowing (ship), that We might make it for you a reminder, and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:11–12].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if We will, We drown them﴾, meaning: those who are in the ships, ﴿then there is no one to cry out for them﴾, i.e., no helper for them against what they are in, ﴿nor are they rescued﴾, i.e., from what has befallen them. ﴿Except as a mercy from Us﴾ — this is an exception of disconnection (istithna' munqati'), its implied sense being: but by Our mercy We let you travel on land and sea, and We allow you to reach a specified term; therefore He said: ﴿and as enjoyment for a time﴾, i.e., until a known time with Allah.

Allah says, informing about the persistence of the polytheists in their misguidance and error, and their indifference to the sins they have committed in the past and to what awaits them before them on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Beware of what is before you and what is behind you, that you may receive mercy,"﴾ Mujahid said: "(What is before you and behind you means) the sins." And others said the opposite. ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾ meaning: perhaps Allah, by your guarding against that, will have mercy on you and grant you security from His punishment. The sense of his statement is: they do not respond to that and turn away from it. He dispensed with that by His saying: ﴿And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord﴾ meaning: [proving] the Oneness (of Allah) and the truthfulness of the messengers, ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾ meaning: they do not reflect upon it and do not benefit from it.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend from what Allah has provided you,"﴾ meaning: and when they are commanded to spend from what Allah has provided them upon the poor and the needy among the Muslims, ﴿those who disbelieve say to those who believe﴾ meaning: concerning the believers among the poor; that is, they say to those among the believers who command them to spend, arguing against them regarding what they were commanded: ﴿Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed?﴾ meaning: these whom you command us to spend upon, if Allah willed, He would have enriched them and fed them from His provision, so we conform to Allah's will concerning them. ﴿You are only in clear error﴾ meaning: in your command to us to do that.

Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that this is from the statement of Allah to the disbelievers when they debated with the Muslims and responded to them, so He said to them: ﴿You are only in clear error﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/9).]], but in this there is room for consideration.

The Most High tells of the disbelievers' disdain for the Hour when they say: ﴿When will this promise be fulfilled, [if you are truthful]?﴾ [[Addition from manuscript A.]] ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾ [Ash-Shura: 18]. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They are only awaiting one blast, which will seize them while they are disputing﴾. That is, they are only awaiting one blast, and this is, Allah knows best, the blast of terror (nafkhat al-faza'). The trumpet (al-sur) will be blown with the blast of terror while people are in their markets and places of livelihood, disputing and quarrelling as is their custom. While they are in this state, Allah the Exalted commands Israfil (Isrāfīl), and he blows into the trumpet a blast which he prolongs and extends. No one on the face of the earth will remain without inclining his ear and raising his neck (laytan, which is the side of the neck), listening for the sound coming from the direction of the sky. Then those who are alive among the people will be driven to the place of gathering on the Day of Resurrection with fire surrounding them from every side. For this reason He says: ﴿So they will not be able to make a bequest﴾, that is, concerning what they possess, since the matter is more important than that, ﴿nor will they return to their families﴾.

Traditions and hadiths related on this matter have been mentioned, which we have cited in another place [[At the commentary on verse 73 of Surat al-An'am.]]. After this there will be the blast of swooning (nafkhat al-sa'q), by which all living beings will die except the Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-Hayy al-Qayyum). After that will be the blast of resurrection (nafkhat al-ba'th).

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 36, verses 59–62:**

Allah the Exalted says, informing of the condition the disbelievers will come to on the Day of Resurrection, through His command to them that they should separate (*imtazu*), meaning: they will be distinguished from the believers in their station, as in His saying: ﴿And on the Day We gather them all, then say to those who associated others with Allah: "Stay in your place, you and your partners." Then We will separate them﴾ [Yunus: 28]. He also says: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, that Day they will be divided﴾ [Ar-Rum: 14], and ﴿That Day they will be separated﴾ [Ar-Rum: 43], meaning they will become two split groups. And ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their wives, and what they used to worship besides Allah, and guide them to the path of the Hellfire﴾ [As-Saffat: 22–23].

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾. This is a rebuke from Allah to the disbelievers among the children of Adam, who obeyed Satan, who is a clear enemy to them, and disobeyed the Most Merciful, who created them and provided for them. Therefore He said: ﴿And that you should worship Me; this is the straight path﴾, meaning: I had commanded you in the life of this world to disobey Satan and to worship Me, and this is the straight path. But you took other than that way and followed Satan in what he commanded you. Therefore He said: ﴿And he had already led astray from among you a great multitude﴾. It is said "*jibillan*" with a kasra on the *jim* and a shaddah on the *lam*, and it is said "*jubulan*" with a damma on the *jim* and *ba'*, and a light *lam*. Some of them pronounce the *ba'* with a sukun. The meaning is a great number of creation, as said by Mujahid, as-Suddi, Qatadah, and Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then did you not use reason?﴾, meaning: Did you not have reason to oppose your Lord in what He commanded you, which is to worship Him alone with no partner, and to turn away from following Satan?

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi', from one who narrated to him, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will command Hell, and a bright and dark mass will emerge from it, and it will say: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you should worship Me; this is the straight path. And he had already led astray from among you a great multitude. Then did you not use reason? This is Hell which you were promised﴾. Then it will say: 'Separate yourselves today, O criminals!' So the people will be separated and will fall to their knees." This is the scene described by Allah the Exalted: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be called to its record: "Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do"﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 28].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 36, verse 63–67:

It will be said to the disbelievers among the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, when Hellfire has been brought forth for them as a rebuke and reproach: ﴿This is Hell which you were promised.﴾ That is: this is the one the messengers warned you about, and you denied them. ﴿Burn therein today for what you used to disbelieve.﴾ As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Day they will be pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent pushing. "This is the Fire which you used to deny. Is this magic, or do you not see?"﴾ [At-Tur: 13-15].

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Today We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.﴾ This is the state of the disbelievers and hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, when they deny what they committed in the world and swear that they did not do it. So Allah seals over their mouths, and He makes their limbs speak of what they did.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Shaybah Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi narrated to us, Abu Amir al-Asadi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ubayd al-Mukattib, from al-Fudayl ibn Amr, from al-Sha'bi, [In T: "al-Nasa'i and Muslim narrated it."] from Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, and he laughed until his molars showed. Then he said: "Do you know what I am laughing at?" We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "At the dispute of the servant with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He will say: 'My Lord [In T, S: "O Lord"], did You not protect me from injustice?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'I do not accept any witness against me except from myself.'

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, has also given its chain a good rating, saying: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'ah, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd al-Hadrami, from a man who narrated to him, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The first bone of a human being to speak on the day the mouths are sealed will be his thigh, from the left leg." [al-Musnad (4/151); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/351): "its chain is good."]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, Yunus ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, who said: Abu Burdah said: Abu Musa — he is al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him — said: The believer will be summoned to reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, and his Lord will present his deeds to him in what is between them, and he will acknowledge them, saying: "Yes, my Lord, I did, I did, I did." Then Allah will forgive him his sins and cover them from him. Then no creature on earth will see any of those sins, and his good deeds will be made to appear, and he will wish that all people could see them. And the disbeliever and the hypocrite will be summoned to reckoning, and his Lord will present his deeds to him, and he will deny them and say: "My Lord, by Your might, this angel has recorded for me what I did not do." The angel will say to him: "Did you not do such and such, on such a day, in such a place?" He will say: "No, by Your might, my Lord, I did not do it." When he does that, his mouth will be sealed. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: I think the first thing to speak from him will be his right thigh. Then he recited: ﴿Today We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari (23/17).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, so they would race for the path, but how could they see?﴾ Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas in its explanation: He says: If We willed, We would have misguided them from guidance, so how could they be guided? Murrah said: We would have blinded them.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: If Allah willed, He would have obliterated their eyes, making them blind, wandering about.

Al-Suddi said: If We willed, We would have blinded their sights.

Mujahid, Abu Salih, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿so they would race for the path﴾ means: the road.

Ibn Zayd said: By the path here is meant the truth. ﴿But how could they see﴾ when We have obliterated their eyes?

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿but how could they see﴾ means: they would not see the truth.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places﴾ al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: We would have destroyed them.

Al-Suddi said: That is, We would have changed their creation.

Abu Salih said: We would have made them into stones.

Al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah said: We would have made them sit on their feet.

For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return﴾ meaning: forward, nor backward; rather they would remain in one state, neither advancing nor retreating.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 36, verse 63–67:

It will be said to the disbelievers among the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, when Hellfire has been brought forth for them as a rebuke and reproach: ﴿This is Hell which you were promised.﴾ That is: this is the one the messengers warned you about, and you denied them. ﴿Burn therein today for what you used to disbelieve.﴾ As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Day they will be pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent pushing. "This is the Fire which you used to deny. Is this magic, or do you not see?"﴾ [At-Tur: 13-15].

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Today We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.﴾ This is the state of the disbelievers and hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, when they deny what they committed in the world and swear that they did not do it. So Allah seals over their mouths, and He makes their limbs speak of what they did.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Shaybah Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi narrated to us, Abu Amir al-Asadi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ubayd al-Mukattib, from al-Fudayl ibn Amr, from al-Sha'bi, [In T: "al-Nasa'i and Muslim narrated it."] from Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, and he laughed until his molars showed. Then he said: "Do you know what I am laughing at?" We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "At the dispute of the servant with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He will say: 'My Lord [In T, S: "O Lord"], did You not protect me from injustice?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'I do not accept any witness against me except from myself.'

He will say: 'Sufficient is yourself as a reckoner against you today, and the noble scribes as witnesses.' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will be told: 'Speak.' So they will speak of his deeds. Then He will leave him free to speak, and he will say: 'Away with you and destruction! It was for you that I was contending.'"

It was also narrated by Muslim and al-Nasa'i, both from Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr, from Abu al-Nadr, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ashja'i, from Sufyan — that is al-Thawri — with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim no. (2969) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11653).] Then al-Nasa'i said: "I do not know anyone who narrated this hadith from Sufyan except al-Ashja'i, and it is a gharib hadith. And Allah knows best."

So he said, but it was previously narrated through Abu Amir Abd al-Malik ibn Amr al-Asadi — who is al-Aqadi — from Sufyan.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Bahz ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "You will be called with your mouths sealed with a seal, and the first thing to be asked about any one of you will be his thigh and his shoulder." It was narrated by al-Nasa'i [Addition from T, S, and al-Sunan al-Kubra] from Muhammad ibn Rafi', from Abd al-Razzaq, with the same.

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the long hadith about the Resurrection, in which he said: "Then he will come to the third and say: 'What are you?' He will say: 'I am Your servant; I believed in You, in Your Prophet, and in Your Book, and I fasted, prayed and gave charity,' praising himself with whatever good he can. Then it will be said to him: 'Shall we send forth our witness against you?' He will think to himself: who could be the one who testifies against him? Then his mouth will be sealed, and his thigh will be told: 'Speak.' So his thigh, his flesh and his bones will speak of what he used to do. That is the hypocrite, and that is so that he may be excused from himself, and that is the one with whom Allah is angry."

Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with it in full.  [Sahih Muslim no. (2968) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4730).]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to us, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, [In T: "Imam Ahmad narrated."] from Uqbah ibn Amir, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The first bone of a human being to speak on the day the mouths are sealed will be his thigh, from the left leg." [In T: "the left."]

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Muhammad ibn Awf, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, with the same.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, has also given its chain a good rating, saying: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'ah, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd al-Hadrami, from a man who narrated to him, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The first bone of a human being to speak on the day the mouths are sealed will be his thigh, from the left leg." [al-Musnad (4/151); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/351): "its chain is good."]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, Yunus ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, who said: Abu Burdah said: Abu Musa — he is al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him — said: The believer will be summoned to reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, and his Lord will present his deeds to him in what is between them, and he will acknowledge them, saying: "Yes, my Lord, I did, I did, I did." Then Allah will forgive him his sins and cover them from him. Then no creature on earth will see any of those sins, and his good deeds will be made to appear, and he will wish that all people could see them. And the disbeliever and the hypocrite will be summoned to reckoning, and his Lord will present his deeds to him, and he will deny them and say: "My Lord, by Your might, this angel has recorded for me what I did not do." The angel will say to him: "Did you not do such and such, on such a day, in such a place?" He will say: "No, by Your might, my Lord, I did not do it." When he does that, his mouth will be sealed. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: I think the first thing to speak from him will be his right thigh. Then he recited: ﴿Today We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari (23/17).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, so they would race for the path, but how could they see?﴾ Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas in its explanation: He says: If We willed, We would have misguided them from guidance, so how could they be guided? Murrah said: We would have blinded them.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: If Allah willed, He would have obliterated their eyes, making them blind, wandering about.

Al-Suddi said: If We willed, We would have blinded their sights.

Mujahid, Abu Salih, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿so they would race for the path﴾ means: the road.

Ibn Zayd said: By the path here is meant the truth. ﴿But how could they see﴾ when We have obliterated their eyes?

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿but how could they see﴾ means: they would not see the truth.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places﴾ al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: We would have destroyed them.

Al-Suddi said: That is, We would have changed their creation.

Abu Salih said: We would have made them into stones.

Al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah said: We would have made them sit on their feet.

For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return﴾ meaning: forward, nor backward; rather they would remain in one state, neither advancing nor retreating.

Ibn Kathir's Commentary on Surah Ya-Sin, verses 68–70 (part 1 of 2)

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the son of Adam that whenever his lifespan is extended, he is returned to weakness after strength, and to incapacity after vigour, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is Allah who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and grey hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 54]. And He said: ﴿And among you is one who is returned to the most decrepit age, so that he knows nothing after having known.﴾ [Al-Hajj: 5].

The purpose of this, and Allah knows best, is to inform us that this world is a abode of cessation and transition, not an abode of permanence and stability. For this reason He said: ﴿Will they not then reason?﴾, meaning: will they not reflect with their minds upon the beginning of their creation, then their passage to youth, then to old age, so that they may know that they were created for another abode, one that has no cessation and from which there is no transition, and from which there is no escape, and that abode is the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾: Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), that He did not teach him poetry, ﴿nor is it befitting for him﴾, meaning it is not in his nature, so he does not excel at it, nor does he love it, nor is his disposition inclined to it. For this reason it is reported that he, upon him be prayers and peace, did not memorise a line of verse in a regular metre; rather, if he recited one, he would break its metre (zihaf, a permitted deviation in Arabic metre) or fail to complete it.

Abu Zur'ah al-Razi said: I was told, from Isma'il ibn Mujalid, from his father, from al-Sha'bi, that he said: "No son or daughter of Abd al-Muttalib was born except that they composed poetry, except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Ibn 'Asakir mentioned this in the biography of "Utbah ibn Abi Lahab," who was eaten by a wolf at al-Zarqa'. [Note: I did not find his biography in the Tarikh Dimashq available to me, nor in the Mukhtasar of Ibn Manzur.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salamah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan (that is, al-Basri), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite this verse:

"Islam and grey hair are sufficient for a man as a restraint."

Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah," [and recited the verse in the correct form]:

"Grey hair and Islam are sufficient for a man as a restraint..."

Abu Bakr, or 'Umar, said: "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah. Allah says: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾." [Note: Ibn Sa'd narrated it in at-Tabaqat (1/382) through 'Arim, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, in a mursal form.]

Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated in ad-Dala'il that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Abbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami: "You are the one who said:

'Would you make my plunder and the plunder of the slaves to be divided between al-Aqra' and 'Uyayna?'"

He said: "It is actually: 'between 'Uyayna and al-Aqra'.'" He said: "It is all the same." [Note: Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (5/181).] That is, in meaning, upon him be the blessings and peace of Allah.

As-Suhayli in ar-Rawd al-Unuf mentioned, regarding this inversion of order that occurred in his speech, upon him be peace, in this verse, a rare explanation whose gist is the nobility of al-Aqra' ibn Habis over 'Uyayna ibn Badr al-Fazari, because the latter apostatised during the days of as-Siddiq, unlike the former. And Allah knows best.

Likewise al-Umawi narrated in his Maghazi that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) walked among the slain on the day of Badr, saying: "We split skulls..................................."

Then as-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, completed the line, saying:

"..... from men who were dear to us, but they were more ungrateful and unjust."

This is a line by one of the poets of the Arabs, from a qasidah of his, and it is in al-Hamasah. [Note: al-Hamasah of Abu Tammam (1/107).]

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, Mughirah narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delayed in receiving news, he would recite in regard to it the line of Tarafah:

"And news will come to you from one you did not provide for."

This was also narrated by an-Nasa'i in al-Yawm wal-Laylah through the route of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from al-Sha'bi, from her. At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i also narrated it, from the hadith of al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh ibn Hani', from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, in the same manner. Then at-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." [Note: Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (2848) and an-Nasa'i in as-Sunan al-Kubra no. (10835). At-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, Usamah narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite from the poetry:

"And news will come to you from one you did not provide for..."

Then he said: It was narrated by others besides Za'idah, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from 'A'ishah. [Note: Ibn Sa'd narrated it in at-Tabaqat (1/383) through al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, who said: 'A'ishah was asked, and he mentioned it in a similar manner.]

This is from the poetry of Tarafah ibn al-'Abd, in his famous mu'allaqah. What is mentioned here is the second half of a line from it, the first of which is:

"Time will reveal to you what you were ignorant of, and news will come to you from one you did not provide for..."

"And news will come to you from one who has not been provided for by you at all, and you have not set for him a time of appointment." [Note: See the Diwan of Tarafah ibn al-'Abd, p. (66).]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Hafs 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn Nu'aym, the agent of al-Muttaqi in Baghdad, narrated to us, Abu Muhammad 'Abdullah ibn Hilal an-Nahwi ad-Darir narrated to us, 'Ali ibn 'Amr al-Ansari narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never combined a line of poetry except one line, [and he said]:

"Be optimistic with what you desire, and it will happen, for rarely is it said of a thing that it did not come to pass once it was hoped for."

[Note: as-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi (7/43). He said: "I have not written it except with this isnad, and among them is one whose condition is unknown."]

I asked our shaykh, al-Hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, about this hadith, and he said: "It is munkar (rejected)." The shaykh of al-Hakim is not known, nor is the blind man.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah: It was said to 'A'ishah: "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ever recite any poetry?" She said: "It was the speech he disliked most. However, he used to recite a line by the brother of Bani Qays, but he would reverse its first half to be last and its last to be first." Abu Bakr said: "It is not like this." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I am not a poet, nor is it befitting for me." Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, and this is the wording of Ibn Abi Hatim. [Note: Tafsir at-Tabari (23/19).]

Ma'mar narrated from Qatadah: It reached me that 'A'ishah was asked: "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ever recite any poetry?" She said: "No, except the line of Tarafah:

'Time will reveal to you what you were ignorant of, and news will come to you from one you did not provide for...'"

And he would say: "...from one who did not provide you with news." Abu Bakr said: "It is not like this." He said: "I am not a poet, nor is it befitting for me." [Note: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it in his Tafsir (2/117) from Ma'mar from Qatadah, with the same content.]

It is established in the two Sahihs that he, upon him be prayers and peace, recited on the day of the digging of the trench verses of 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah, but as a follow-up to the words of his companions, for they would chant rajaz (a metre of verse) while digging, saying:

"O Allah, had it not been for You we would not have been guided, nor would we have given charity nor prayed..."

"So send down tranquillity upon us, and make our feet firm if we meet (the enemy)..."

"Indeed, those who have transgressed against us, when they desire strife, we refuse..."

And he would raise his voice with his words "refuse" and prolong it. [Note: Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7236) and Sahih Muslim no. (1803), from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him.] This has also been narrated in the Sahih with a zihaf (deviation in metre). Likewise it is established that he said on the day of Hunayn, while riding the mule, advancing it into the chests of the enemy:

"I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib." [Note: Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2864) and Sahih Muslim no. (1776).]

But they said: This occurred by coincidence, without intent to a poetic metre, rather it flowed upon the tongue without deliberate intention.

Likewise what is established in the two Sahihs from Jundub ibn 'Abdullah, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a cave, and his finger was struck, so he said:

"Are you but a finger that bled, and in the way of Allah what you have suffered?" [Note: Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2802) and Sahih Muslim no. (1796).]

It will come at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except for minor faults﴾ [An-Najm: 32], the recitation of:

"If You forgive, O Allah, You forgive much, and which of Your servants has not transgressed?"

All of this does not contradict his, upon him be peace, not having been taught poetry and it not being befitting for him; for Allah, exalted is He, only taught him the Great Qur'an, which ﴿falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from One Wise and Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42]. It is not poetry, as a group of foolish disbelievers of Quraysh claimed, nor is it soothsaying, nor fabrication, nor magic that deceives, as the statements of the misguided and the opinions of the ignorant have varied concerning it. His disposition, upon him be peace, was by nature and by law averse to the craft of poetry, as Abu Dawud narrated, saying:

Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Shurahbil ibn Yazid al-Ma'afiri narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi' at-Tanukhi, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr say: [I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say]: "I do not care what I am given if I drink a remedy, or hang an amulet, or recite poetry from my own self." Abu Dawud alone narrated it. [Note: Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3869).]

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Shayban, from Abu Nawfal, who said: I asked 'A'ishah: "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) listen to poetry in his presence?" She said: "It was the speech he disliked most." And from 'A'ishah he also said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) liked comprehensive supplications and left aside what was between them." [Note: al-Musnad (6/148).]

Abu Dawud said: Abu al-Walid at-Tayalisi narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "That the belly of one of you be filled with pus is better for him than that it be filled with poetry." He alone narrated it through this route, and its isnad is on the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it. [Note: Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5009).]

And Imam Ahmad said: Buraid narrated to us, Qaza'ah ibn Suwayd al-Bahili narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Makhlad, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani (ḥ). And al-Ashyab narrated to us and said: from Ibn 'Asim, from [Abu] [[Addition from manuscripts T, S, and al-Musnad.]] al-Ash'ath [[In T: "Imam Ahmad narrated with his isnad".]] from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever composes a line of poetry after the late night prayer ('isha'), his prayer that night will not be accepted from him." [[al-Musnad (4/125).]] This is a gharib (unusual) hadith through this chain, and none of the authors of the Six Books narrated it. What is meant by this is composing poetry, not reciting it, and Allah knows best. Yet poetry includes what is permissible, namely satire against the polytheists, which the poets of Islam practised, such as Hassan ibn Thabit, Ka'b ibn Malik, 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah, and their like, may Allah be pleased with them all. And it includes poetry containing wisdom, admonitions and good manners, as is found in the poetry of a group from the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era), among them Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt, about whom the Prophet ﷺ said: "His poetry believed, but his heart disbelieved." [[Narrated by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr in al-Tamhid (4/7) through the route of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Some of the Companions recited a hundred verses of his to the Prophet ﷺ, and after each verse he would say: "Hihi" (go on), meaning he was asking him for more, so he would recite more of it. [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2255), from the hadith of al-Sharid, may Allah be pleased with him.]]
Abu Dawud also narrated from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Buraidah ibn al-Husayb [[In manuscript A: "al-Khusayf".]], and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, some eloquence is magic, and indeed some poetry contains wisdom." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. (5010–5012).]]
Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry﴾, meaning: Muhammad ﷺ, Allah did not teach him poetry. ﴿Nor is it befitting for him﴾, i.e., it is not suitable for him. ﴿It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾, i.e., this which We have taught him is nothing but a reminder and a clear Qur'an, i.e., plain, evident and manifest to whoever contemplates and reflects upon it. Therefore He said: ﴿to warn whoever is alive﴾, i.e., this clear Qur'an warns every living person upon the face of the earth, as in His saying: ﴿that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ (Al-An'am: 19), and His saying: ﴿And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ (Hud: 17). The one who benefits from its warning is only the one whose heart is alive and whose insight is illuminated, as Qatadah said: "Alive of heart, alive of sight." Al-Dahhak said: "Meaning: one who is rational." ﴿And the word will be justified against the disbelievers﴾, i.e., it is a mercy to the believer and a proof against the disbeliever.

Ibn Kathir's Commentary on Surah Ya-Sin, verses 68–70 (part 1 of 2)

Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Shurahbil ibn Yazid al-Ma'afiri narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi' at-Tanukhi, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr say: [I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say]: "I do not care what I am given if I drink a remedy, or hang an amulet, or recite poetry from my own self." Abu Dawud alone narrated it. [Note: Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3869).]

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Shayban, from Abu Nawfal, who said: I asked 'A'ishah: "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) listen to poetry in his presence?" She said: "It was the speech he disliked most." And from 'A'ishah he also said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) liked comprehensive supplications and left aside what was between them." [Note: al-Musnad (6/148).]

Abu Dawud said: Abu al-Walid at-Tayalisi narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "That the belly of one of you be filled with pus is better for him than that it be filled with poetry." He alone narrated it through this route, and its isnad is on the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it. [Note: Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5009).]

And Imam Ahmad said: Buraid narrated to us, Qaza'ah ibn Suwayd al-Bahili narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Makhlad, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani (ḥ). And al-Ashyab narrated to us and said: from Ibn 'Asim, from [Abu] [[Addition from manuscripts T, S, and al-Musnad.]] al-Ash'ath [[In T: "Imam Ahmad narrated with his isnad".]] from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever composes a line of poetry after the late night prayer ('isha'), his prayer that night will not be accepted from him." [[al-Musnad (4/125).]] This is a gharib (unusual) hadith through this chain, and none of the authors of the Six Books narrated it. What is meant by this is composing poetry, not reciting it, and Allah knows best. Yet poetry includes what is permissible, namely satire against the polytheists, which the poets of Islam practised, such as Hassan ibn Thabit, Ka'b ibn Malik, 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah, and their like, may Allah be pleased with them all. And it includes poetry containing wisdom, admonitions and good manners, as is found in the poetry of a group from the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era), among them Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt, about whom the Prophet ﷺ said: "His poetry believed, but his heart disbelieved." [[Narrated by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr in al-Tamhid (4/7) through the route of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Some of the Companions recited a hundred verses of his to the Prophet ﷺ, and after each verse he would say: "Hihi" (go on), meaning he was asking him for more, so he would recite more of it. [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2255), from the hadith of al-Sharid, may Allah be pleased with him.]]
Abu Dawud also narrated from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Buraidah ibn al-Husayb [[In manuscript A: "al-Khusayf".]], and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, some eloquence is magic, and indeed some poetry contains wisdom." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. (5010–5012).]]
Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry﴾, meaning: Muhammad ﷺ, Allah did not teach him poetry. ﴿Nor is it befitting for him﴾, i.e., it is not suitable for him. ﴿It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾, i.e., this which We have taught him is nothing but a reminder and a clear Qur'an, i.e., plain, evident and manifest to whoever contemplates and reflects upon it. Therefore He said: ﴿to warn whoever is alive﴾, i.e., this clear Qur'an warns every living person upon the face of the earth, as in His saying: ﴿that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ (Al-An'am: 19), and His saying: ﴿And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ (Hud: 17). The one who benefits from its warning is only the one whose heart is alive and whose insight is illuminated, as Qatadah said: "Alive of heart, alive of sight." Al-Dahhak said: "Meaning: one who is rational." ﴿And the word will be justified against the disbelievers﴾, i.e., it is a mercy to the believer and a proof against the disbeliever.

Ibn Kathir said, mentioning what Allah has bestowed upon His creatures from these livestock which He has subjected to them: ﴿So they are their owners﴾. Qatadah said: "Capable of them" (in one version, "obedient to them"). That is, He made them able to subdue them, while they are submissive to them and do not resist them. Indeed, if a child came to a camel, it would make it kneel; and if he wished, he could make it stand and drive it, and it would be docile and led by him. Likewise, even if the caravan were a hundred camels or more, all of them would travel at the pace of a small child.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And from them is their ride, and from them they eat﴾: that is, some of them they ride on during journeys, and they carry loads on them to all regions and lands. ﴿And from them they eat﴾: when they wish, they slaughter and eat them.

﴿And for them therein are benefits﴾: that is, from their wool, fur and hair, they make furnishings and goods for a time. ﴿And drinks﴾: that is, from their milk and urine, for whoever seeks treatment, and the like. ﴿Will they not then be grateful?﴾ That is: will they not affirm the Oneness of the Creator and Subjector of these, and not associate anyone else with Him?

Allah the Exalted says, rebuking the polytheists for taking rivals (andad) as gods besides Allah, hoping thereby that those gods would help them, provide for them, and bring them near to Allah in closeness (zulfa).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They cannot help them﴾. That is, the gods are not able to help their worshippers. Rather, they are weaker than that, less, more humble, more contemptible, and more insignificant, and they cannot even defend themselves or take revenge against one who intends them harm, because they are inanimate objects that neither hear nor understand.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿while they are a host brought up before them﴾. Mujahid said: it means at the reckoning. He intends that these idols will be gathered together on the Day of Resurrection, brought forward before the reckoning of their worshippers, so that this will be more emphatic in their humiliation and more evident as proof against them in establishing the argument over them.

Qatadah said: ﴿They cannot help them﴾ means the gods, ﴿while they are a host brought up before them﴾. The polytheists become angry for the gods in this world, while the gods do not bring them any good nor ward off any evil from them; they are only idols.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said the same. This view is good, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So do not let their speech grieve you﴾, that is, their denial of you and their disbelief in Allah. ﴿Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they reveal﴾. That is, We know all that they are upon, and We will recompense them for their description and deal with them accordingly on the Day when they will not lose any of their deeds, whether great or small, minor or major; rather, all that they used to do, old and new, will be presented to them.

Mujahid, Ikrimah, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, al-Suddi and Qatadah said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf [may Allah curse him] [[addition from S, A.]] came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ holding a decayed bone, which he was crumbling and scattering into the air [[in A: "scattering it"]], and he said: "O Muhammad, do you claim that Allah will resurrect this?" He said: "Yes. Allah will cause you to die, then resurrect you, then gather you to the Fire." And these verses were revealed at the end of Surah Ya-Sin: ﴿Does not man see that We created him from a drop of semen?﴾ to the end of them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us, Uthman ibn Said al-Zayyat narrated to us, from Hushaym, from Abu Bishr, from Said ibn Jubayr [[in T: "Ibn Abi Hatim related with his chain"]], from Ibn Abbas, that al-As [[in T, S, A: "al-As"]] ibn Wa'il took a bone from the gravel, crumbled it with his hand, and then said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Will Allah bring this to life after it has become like this?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes. Allah will cause you to die, then bring you to life, then enter you into Hell." He said: And the verses at the end of Surah Ya-Sin were revealed.

Ibn Jarir related it from Yaqub ibn Ibrahim, from Hushaym, from Abu Bishr, from Said ibn Jubayr, and he mentioned it without mentioning "Ibn Abbas" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/21)]].

It is also narrated through al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy came with a bone, crumbled it, and he mentioned something similar to what preceded.

This is munkar, because the surah is Meccan, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was only in Medina. In any case, whether these verses were revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf, or al-As ibn Wa'il, or both of them, they are general in application to everyone who denies the resurrection. The alif and lam in His saying ﴿Does not man see﴾ are for the category, encompassing every denier of the resurrection.

﴿That We created him from a drop of semen, and behold, he is a clear adversary﴾ meaning: Has not the one who denies the resurrection reasoned from the beginning to the return? For Allah began the creation of man from an extract of despised water, creating him from a weak, lowly, despised thing, as He said: ﴿Did We not create you from a despised water? Then We placed it in a firm abode, for a known term﴾ [al-Mursalat: 20-22]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a drop of mingled fluid, that We may try him﴾ [al-Insan: 2], meaning from a drop of mixed, dispersed fluids. So the One who created him from this weak drop is surely able to return him after his death? As Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad:

Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Harīz narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah narrated to me, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Busr ibn Jahhash, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spat one day into his palm, placed his finger upon it, and then said: "Allah the Exalted says: 'Son of Adam, how can you outdo Me when I created you from the like of this? When I had proportioned and balanced you, you walked between your two garments, and the earth had a rumble from you. Then you gathered and withheld, until when the collarbones reached (the throat), you said: "I will give charity," and how can there be a time for charity?'"

Ibn Majah narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Jarir ibn Uthman, with the same [[Musnad (4/310) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2707); al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/364): "Its chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy."]]. For this reason He said: ﴿And he makes for Us a comparison and forgets his own creation. He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ That is, he deemed unlikely the restoration by Allah the Exalted, the One of great power who created the heavens and the earth, of bodies and decayed bones, and forgot himself, and that Allah created him from nothing. So he knew of himself what is greater than what he deemed unlikely, denied and rejected. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "He will give them life who brought them into being the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation."﴾ That is, He knows the bones in all regions and corners of the earth, wherever they went, and wherever they were scattered and torn apart.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Rib'i, who said: Uqbah ibn Amr said to Hudhayfah: "Will you not tell us what you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "I heard him say: 'A man was present at death, and when he despaired of life he instructed his family: "When I die, gather for me a great quantity of firewood, then kindle a fire in it, until it has consumed my flesh and reached my bones and they have been burned. Then take them, crush them, and scatter them into the sea."' They did so, and Allah gathered him and said to him: 'Why did you do that?' He said: 'Out of fear of You.' So Allah forgave him.'" Uqbah ibn Amr said: "I too heard him say that, and he was a grave-robber." [[Musnad (5/395)]]

Both Bukhari and Muslim also reported it from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, with many wordings [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6480) and Sahih Muslim no. (2756)]], among them: that he commanded his sons to burn him, then pound him, then scatter half of him on land and half in the sea, on a windy day, meaning one with much wind. They did so. Then Allah commanded the sea to gather what was in it, and commanded the land to gather what was in it, and then said to him: "Be." And behold, he was a standing man. He said to him: "What led you to do what you did?" He said: "Fear of You, and You know best." So He forgave him.

* *

His saying: ﴿He who made for you fire from the green tree, so that from it you kindle﴾ meaning: He who began the creation of this tree from water until it became green and fresh, bearing fruit and ripeness, then returned it until it became dry firewood with which fire is kindled, is likewise the Doer of what He wills, able to do whatever He intends, and nothing prevents Him.

Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿He who made for you fire from the green tree, so that from it you kindle﴾: He who brought this fire out of this tree is able to resurrect it.

It has also been said that what is meant is the wood of al-Markh and al-Affar, which grows in the land of the Hijaz. Whoever wishes to strike fire and has no flint takes from it two green sticks and strikes one against the other, and fire is produced between them, just like a flint. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. And in the proverb: "For every tree there is fire, and al-Markh and al-Affar have been made excellent." And the wise have said: "In every tree there is fire except the ghab [[in A: "al-ataab"]]."
