When Allah intends a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.

[[See the verse of poetry at the commentary on verse 40 of Surat an-Nahl.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Musa ibn al-Musayyab narrated to us, from Shahr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah says: O My servants, all of you are sinners except those whom I have pardoned, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you. All of you are needy except those whom I have enriched. Indeed I am Generous, Glorious, Finder, doing what I will. My giving is speech, and My punishment is speech. When I intend a thing, I only say to it, 'Be,' and it is." [[Musnad (5/177).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿So Glorified is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned﴾ means: exaltation, sanctification, and declaration of freedom from every imperfection, to the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth, to whom all affairs return, to whom belong the creation and the command, and to whom the servants will be returned on the Day of Resurrection, where He will recompense every doer for his deed, and He is the Just, the Bountiful.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿So Glorified is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things﴾ is like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say, "In whose hand is the dominion of all things?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 88] [[In one manuscript: "Say, in whose hand is the dominion of all things and to Him you will be returned," which is an error.]], and like His saying: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion﴾ [al-Mulk: 1]. So al-Mulk (dominion) and al-Malakut (sovereignty) are the same in meaning, like rahmah and rahamut, rahbah and rahabut, and jabr and jabarut. Some people claimed that al-mulk is the world of bodies and al-malakut is the world of spirits, but the first view is the correct one, and it is what the majority of the exegetes and others hold.

Imam Ahmad said: Hammad narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, who said: my paternal cousin of Hudhayfah narrated to me, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I stood in prayer with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night, and he recited the seven long surahs in seven rak'ahs. Whenever he raised his head from bowing, he said: "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah." Then he said: "Al-hamdu li-dhi al-malakut wal-jabarut wal-kibriya' wal-azamah" (Praise belongs to the Possessor of sovereignty, power, majesty and greatness). His bowing was as long as his standing, and his prostration was as long as his bowing, and I finished while my legs were almost breaking. [[Musnad (5/388).]]

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi in al-Shama'il, and al-Nasa'i have also related, through the narration of Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Hamzah, mawla of the Ansar, from a man of Banu Abs, from Hudhayfah, that he saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at night, and he would say: "Allahu Akbar" three times, "Dhu al-malakut wal-jabarut wal-kibriya' wal-azamah." Then he began and recited al-Baqarah, then bowed, and his bowing was about as long as his standing, and in his bowing he would say: "Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim." Then he raised his head from bowing, and his standing was about as long as his bowing, and he would say: "Li-Rabbi al-hamd." Then he prostrated, and his prostration was about as long as his standing, and in his prostration he would say: "Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la." Then he raised his head from prostration, and he would sit between the two prostrations for about as long as his prostration, and he would say: "Rabbi, ighfir li, Rabbi ighfir li." He prayed four rak'ahs, reciting in them al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa' and al-Ma'idah or al-An'am (Shu'bah was uncertain). This is the wording of Abu Dawud. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (874), al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi no. (260), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/199).]]

al-Nasa'i said: "Abu Hamzah, in our view, is Talhah ibn Yazid, and this man resembles being a connection (silah)." So he said. The more likely view is that he is the paternal cousin of Hudhayfah, as mentioned earlier in the narration of Imam Ahmad, [and Allah knows best]. Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Amr ibn Qays, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who said: I stood in prayer with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night, and he stood and recited Surat al-Baqarah. He did not pass any verse of mercy without pausing to ask, and did not pass any verse of punishment without pausing to seek refuge. He said: Then he bowed for as long as his standing, saying in his bowing: "Subhana dhi al-jabarut wal-malakut wal-kibriya' wal-azamah." Then he prostrated for as long as his standing, and said in his prostration the same. Then he stood and recited Al 'Imran, then recited surah after surah.

al-Tirmidhi in al-Shama'il and al-Nasa'i related it through the narration of Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, with the same chain. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (873), al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi no. (296), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/191).]]

[End of the commentary on Surat Ya-Sin. All praise is due to Allah, first and last, outwardly and inwardly.]

[End of the commentary on Surat Ya-Sin. All praise is due to Allah, first and last, outwardly and inwardly.]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, alerting to His great power in creating the seven heavens, with the wandering planets and the fixed stars that are in them, and the seven earths and what is in them of mountains and sand, seas and deserts, and what lies between these; and guiding to the reasoning for the resurrection of bodies by the creation of these great things, as in His saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57]. And here He said: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ meaning: the likes of mankind, so that He would restore them as He originated them. This was said by Ibn Jarir [[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/21).]].

This verse is like His saying: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is Able to do all things﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 33], and His saying: ﴿Yes, and He is the Creator, the All-Knowing. His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81–82], meaning: He commands a thing with a single command, which needs no repetition:

When Allah intends a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.

[[See the verse of poetry at the commentary on verse 40 of Surat an-Nahl.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Musa ibn al-Musayyab narrated to us, from Shahr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah says: O My servants, all of you are sinners except those whom I have pardoned, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you. All of you are needy except those whom I have enriched. Indeed I am Generous, Glorious, Finder, doing what I will. My giving is speech, and My punishment is speech. When I intend a thing, I only say to it, 'Be,' and it is." [[Musnad (5/177).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿So Glorified is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned﴾ means: exaltation, sanctification, and declaration of freedom from every imperfection, to the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth, to whom all affairs return, to whom belong the creation and the command, and to whom the servants will be returned on the Day of Resurrection, where He will recompense every doer for his deed, and He is the Just, the Bountiful.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿So Glorified is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things﴾ is like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say, "In whose hand is the dominion of all things?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 88] [[In one manuscript: "Say, in whose hand is the dominion of all things and to Him you will be returned," which is an error.]], and like His saying: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion﴾ [al-Mulk: 1]. So al-Mulk (dominion) and al-Malakut (sovereignty) are the same in meaning, like rahmah and rahamut, rahbah and rahabut, and jabr and jabarut. Some people claimed that al-mulk is the world of bodies and al-malakut is the world of spirits, but the first view is the correct one, and it is what the majority of the exegetes and others hold.

Imam Ahmad said: Hammad narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, who said: my paternal cousin of Hudhayfah narrated to me, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I stood in prayer with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night, and he recited the seven long surahs in seven rak'ahs. Whenever he raised his head from bowing, he said: "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah." Then he said: "Al-hamdu li-dhi al-malakut wal-jabarut wal-kibriya' wal-azamah" (Praise belongs to the Possessor of sovereignty, power, majesty and greatness). His bowing was as long as his standing, and his prostration was as long as his bowing, and I finished while my legs were almost breaking. [[Musnad (5/388).]]

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi in al-Shama'il, and al-Nasa'i have also related, through the narration of Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Hamzah, mawla of the Ansar, from a man of Banu Abs, from Hudhayfah, that he saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at night, and he would say: "Allahu Akbar" three times, "Dhu al-malakut wal-jabarut wal-kibriya' wal-azamah." Then he began and recited al-Baqarah, then bowed, and his bowing was about as long as his standing, and in his bowing he would say: "Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim." Then he raised his head from bowing, and his standing was about as long as his bowing, and he would say: "Li-Rabbi al-hamd." Then he prostrated, and his prostration was about as long as his standing, and in his prostration he would say: "Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la." Then he raised his head from prostration, and he would sit between the two prostrations for about as long as his prostration, and he would say: "Rabbi, ighfir li, Rabbi ighfir li." He prayed four rak'ahs, reciting in them al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa' and al-Ma'idah or al-An'am (Shu'bah was uncertain). This is the wording of Abu Dawud. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (874), al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi no. (260), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/199).]]

al-Nasa'i said: "Abu Hamzah, in our view, is Talhah ibn Yazid, and this man resembles being a connection (silah)." So he said. The more likely view is that he is the paternal cousin of Hudhayfah, as mentioned earlier in the narration of Imam Ahmad, [and Allah knows best]. As for the narration of Silah ibn Zufar from Hudhayfah, it is in Sahih Muslim, but it does not contain the mention of al-malakut, al-jabarut, al-kibriya' and al-azamah.

Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Amr ibn Qays, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who said: I stood in prayer with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night, and he stood and recited Surat al-Baqarah. He did not pass any verse of mercy without pausing to ask, and did not pass any verse of punishment without pausing to seek refuge. He said: Then he bowed for as long as his standing, saying in his bowing: "Subhana dhi al-jabarut wal-malakut wal-kibriya' wal-azamah." Then he prostrated for as long as his standing, and said in his prostration the same. Then he stood and recited Al 'Imran, then recited surah after surah.

al-Tirmidhi in al-Shama'il and al-Nasa'i related it through the narration of Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, with the same chain. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (873), al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi no. (296), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/191).]]

[End of the commentary on Surat Ya-Sin. All praise is due to Allah, first and last, outwardly and inwardly.]
